Standalone live probe script (not a vitest file) that drives a tool loop against the Codex websocket-cached transport and prints transport, cache and latency statistics.
The legacy API registry still dispatches unknown providers, and the request apiKey reaches the registered api implementation.
TypeBox schema defaults: each API schema keeps its own defaults and the provider superset must NOT inherit any API-specific default.
Grammar and strict JSON-schema constrained sampling: conversion, a hard throw when a require tool hits an adapter without strict support, and grammar tool-call deltas reassembled into arguments.
Context estimation prefers the last valid assistant usage report and estimates only the tail at 3.5 chars per token; a usage older than a later inserted message is ignored (#10497).
Live per-provider overflow sweep: every provider must return stopReason error with a context-too-large message and isContextOverflow() must agree, including a local llama.cpp case.
Live cross-provider handoff matrix: each provider/model generates a small context with thinking plus tool call, then every target model must consume the concatenation of all of them.
Binary PNG fixture: a 200x200 white image with a solid red circle, used by the image-input and tool-result-image tests. Opened and viewed rather than read as text.
Live sweep of degenerate inputs (empty content array, empty string, whitespace-only, empty assistant message in history) that must degrade gracefully rather than throw.
Env key resolution: generic GITHUB_TOKEN and GH_TOKEN are NOT Copilot credentials, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is reported but never returned as an API key, and ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN is.

The shared error-body normalizer handles Mistral, openai APIError, @google/genai and AWS ServiceException shapes, refuses to serialize a response stream body, and truncates to MAX_PROVIDER_ERROR_BODY_CHARS.
EventStream ordering guarantees (buffered events drain in order, later pushes are ignored after completion, waiting consumers wake in registration order) and durationMs stamping rules.
The in-process faux provider: scripted responses, usage estimation, per-model reasoning, tool-call deltas, abort mid-toolcall (no toolcall_end), and unregister semantics.
The per-request fetch option must reach every adapter; the Google adapters refuse a custom fetch explicitly instead of silently bypassing it, but accept globalThis.fetch passed explicitly.

Runs the real model generator against a mocked models.dev catalog and asserts upstream effort metadata wins over the hardcoded maps, and that a newly cataloged effort model automatically gets native effort.
Fireworks catalog wiring: which models use the Anthropic-compatible Messages API, which use OpenAI-completions, and that unsupported long cache retention is omitted.
The strict generator fails BEFORE mutating any generated file when a model id would disappear, and the generated files are byte-identical before and after the failure.
Copilot Claude over Anthropic Messages: Bearer auth, Copilot static and dynamic headers, adaptive thinking effort overrides, and no interleaved-thinking beta.
Copilot device-code login, the model and policy endpoint sequence, and the slow_down polling cadence (5s then 15s) under fake timers.
Classifies HTTP 413 (nested or flat body) as a context overflow through the real SDK, while a 400 with the same body is not, and usage stays zero.
Gemini finish reasons are preserved raw, provider chunks are forwarded to onProviderStreamEvent in order, and the User-Agent defaults to pi but is overridable.
JSON Schema meta keys are stripped recursively without mutating the source schema, $ref is preserved, and Gemini 3 strict tools use VALIDATED function calling.
Gemini 3 tool call ids survive the round trip, unsigned tool calls get no skip_thought_signature_validator, and requiresToolCallId is gated per model.
Image tool results are nested inside functionResponse for Gemini 3 but split into a synthetic turn for Gemini 2.x, and whitespace-only tool text becomes empty output (#8720).
retryGoogleRequest retries a headers-less SDK error with a retryable status, does nothing when maxRetries is unset, and does not retry a non-retryable status.
An empty text/thinking block is dropped only when it is UNSIGNED; a signed empty block is kept so its thoughtSignature can be echoed back, and a signature from another model is dropped.
Live check that thinking is really off for Anthropic, Gemini 2.5 and 3.x, Vertex and OpenRouter: zero thinking events, no thinking block in the content, and the answer still complete.
thinkingLevelMap resolution for Google and Vertex: mapped levels, level-to-token-budget conversion, and that the mapped level also picks the token budget.
Only part.thought === true marks thinking (a bare thoughtSignature does not), and a signature is retained across deltas that omit it.
Placeholder apiKey markers (and GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY placeholders) fall back to ADC, and a custom baseUrl already carrying an apiVersion is not given a second one.
The client identity: PI_AI_VERSION must equal package.json version, the User-Agent format, attribution opt-in, and the per-provider header (for example x-opencode-session) rules.
The OpenRouter catalog builder splits one id into separate chat and image entries, drops models that neither support tools nor emit images, and emits decision models as classifiers.
Live E2E that a tool result containing ONLY an image reaches the model and can be described (colour and shape) by every image-capable provider.
The model registry discriminates chat, image and classifier entries, resolves per-model credentials for both a chat and an image model, and exposes one credential for both.
Live image generation through OpenRouter: a basic generation and an image-to-image variation using the red-circle fixture.
Live check that the model thinks again before the SECOND tool call (thinking present in both turns), for Anthropic and Bedrock.
Streaming JSON keeps an invalid backslash-u escape as literal text instead of dropping the field, and malformed tool arguments never keep the valid prefix (#10868, #10897).
Kimi device-authorization login: poll timing with waitBeforeFirstPoll, temporarily_unavailable retried, invalid_grant not retried, and refresh behaviour.
transformMessages is the lax choke point: null or missing content on user, assistant and toolResult messages normalizes to an empty array instead of crashing (#6259, #6276).
Spawns node with a module resolve hook and asserts importing the root barrel, the compat entrypoint and even building all builtin providers loads ZERO provider SDKs.

The local llama.cpp classifier: it tokenizes, applies the chat template and scores the next token log-probabilities per label, then turns them into choice, score and bool answers with TypeSafe-style confidence.
The max and xhigh reasoning levels are opt-in per model via thinkingLevelMap, a HOLE between high and max is supported, and clampThinkingLevel falls back to the nearest supported level.
ToolResultMessage details must be a JsonValue; non-JSON detail types (any, undefined arrays, callbacks, Date) are rejected at the type level.
Meta device flow plus a second step that mints a Model API key from the identity token, and re-mints on refresh; a missing key reports the setup URL.
Asserts the exact Mistral wire body built from SDK-style options, bytewise SSE handling, timeout behaviour, and that an HTTP 403 keeps both status and body in the error.
Mistral finish reasons are kept raw; an unknown finish reason becomes a non-retryable provider error while error is retryable (#10487).
Reasoning control selection per model family: prompt_mode for Magistral, reasoning_effort for the others, unsupported levels clamped, effort none when thinking is off.
TypeBox symbol keys must be stripped from the tool parameters before the Mistral SDK validates the schema, recursively, or it fails with Input validation failed.
Compile-time assertions that the grouped model data still yields literal api, id and provider types for xAI and GitHub Copilot models.
Pricing: OpenRouter prompt-length overrides become tiers, missing base rates are kept, time-of-day overrides are ignored, and Vercel AI Gateway brackets become tiers.
The published model-data directory is validated against a manifest (schema version, generation timestamp, exact model ids, aggregator and shard agreement) before it is trusted.
Chat models without a type field work through a handwritten provider, mixed lists narrow with isModelType, and stored models of an unknown type are DROPPED rather than failing the refresh.
The lightweight models entry must run a full faux completion with TypeBox, the catalogs and every SDK forbidden from being loaded.

The Models runtime: credential metadata without secrets, auth resolution and refresh, provider registration, model refresh and error maps, deferred fetch and cancel, and unknown providers yielding an error stream.
HTTP proxy resolution honours NO_PROXY (including wildcards, IPv6 and host:port), prefers scoped env aliases, and refuses SOCKS and PAC URLs with a named message.
Every OAuth adapter derives its apiKey from the access token, GitHub Copilot derives its baseUrl from the token proxy endpoint, and the extension OAuth barrel stays free of built-in flows.
The loopback OAuth callback server: wrong path 404, state mismatch 400 with an HTML page, POST 404, and a successful page that names the provider.
Device-code polling cadence: immediate first poll or a wait, slow_down adding 5 seconds when the server gives no interval, a server interval winning, and abort cancelling the wait.
Test helper resolving an API key from the pi agent auth.json, refreshing an expired OAuth credential through the provider flow and saving it back.
ChatGPT OAuth registers a user-owned client, stores the issued client id and granted scopes, and refreshes 3 minutes early.
Live Codex SSE request with aligned cache-affinity identifiers (session id reused as the cache key).
The Codex device-code and browser flows, including the manual-paste path and the account id carried in the access token.

The Codex transport: SSE and websocket-cached modes, cache affinity headers and prompt_cache_key, websocket fallback on connect timeout or idle, connection-age recycling, delta-only continuation with previous_response_id, zstd request compression, and retry-delay limits.
Anthropic-style cache markers on an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, moved onto the trailing tool result when the turn ends with one, and removed entirely when cache retention is off.
An empty tools array must never be serialized as tools: [] (some OpenAI-compatible backends 400 on it), while a turn that genuinely had a tool call still sends tools: [].
prompt_cache_key and prompt_cache_retention for direct OpenAI requests, and the session-affinity headers, with explicit caller headers overriding the generated ones.
Provider chunks, including OpenRouter metadata, are exposed verbatim through onProviderStreamEvent (#9784).
The OpenAI finish_reason is preserved raw next to the normalized stopReason, including content_filter as a provider error.
reasoning_details (encrypted, text, summary) are carried into the thinking signature and replayed, and a delta carrying both reasoning and content orders thinking before text (#10926).
A router model keeps model = the requested id and exposes the routed concrete id in responseModel; an echoing or empty chunk.model leaves responseModel undefined.
SDK retries are disabled by default; the provider-level retry honours retry-after-ms, and a server-requested delay above the limit fails immediately instead of sleeping.
For an adapter that requires thinking as text, a same-model thinking block is replayed as an assistant text part and the request reaches the endpoint.
The thinking token budget is clamped to the response ceiling (minus 1024), xhigh and max clamp to the high budget, and a named budget field wins over the boolean alias.

tool_choice forwarding, finish_reason requirement (a stream ending with only null finish_reason chunks is an error unless the compat flag disables it), tool-call delta coalescing by index, and per-provider reasoning payload shapes.
Tool-result images are batched into a trailing user message after consecutive tool results, empty text parts are dropped, and whitespace-only tool output becomes the (no tool output) placeholder.
compat.vllmPriority is sent as the top-level priority request field and omitted when unset.
The OpenAI Decisions classifier maps choice, score and bool questions to the wire shape, matches answers back by NAME rather than order, and prices usage.
Live direct OpenAI Responses request with aligned cache-affinity identifiers.
A ChatGPT sign-in token rejects max_output_tokens, temperature and prompt_cache_retention, so those fields are omitted, while an API key keeps them.
Provider defaults for the Responses API: reasoning omitted when not requested, tool_choice forwarded, session-affinity headers, and supportsMaxOutputTokens gating max_output_tokens.
Whitespace-only tool result text becomes the (no tool output) placeholder in function_call_output.
A 400+ character foreign Copilot tool item id is hashed into a bounded fc_<hash> id that satisfies the Codex naming rules.
Fallback message ids for multiple text blocks in one assistant turn are unique (msg_pi_1, msg_pi_1_1).
Mid-conversation effort: the reasoning effort stays constant and only a configuration_update input item is appended when the level changes, and it is skipped when the compat flag is off.
Tool-call namespaces received only on output_item.done round-trip for both function and custom tool calls, and are dropped for targets that cannot replay the load items.
partialJson is removed from the persisted tool-call block at output_item.done, and malformed final arguments are marked rather than keeping the parsed prefix.
Live: reasoning-only history after an aborted turn, and a same-provider different-model handoff with tool calls, must not 400 on an orphaned reasoning item.
The Responses stream needs a terminal event: an early EOF is an error, an incomplete response carries a rawStopReason, and a failed terminal event rejects with the provider error.
Tool-result images stay inside the function_call_output item (text plus input_image) and are NOT lifted into a later user message.
A ChatGPT subscription usage-limit error, whether returned as an HTTP 429 or as a failed stream event, links to the ChatGPT usage page.
The OpenCode session header is mapped from sessionId for both stream paths and a case-insensitive caller override is preserved; no header is fabricated without a sessionId (#9326).
The OpenRouter Anthropic latest aliases keep the anthropic cache-control format on the completions API.
Live repro asserting cache_write_tokens survives the openai-completions stream path when an explicit cache_control marker is added to the last user message.
Image generation through OpenRouter returns text plus images, honours the abort signal, and asks for the image modality only for image-only models.
OpenRouter PKCE on a one-shot loopback callback exchanging the code for a permanent API key, with the callback host configurable by env.
OpenRouter reasoning metadata becomes a thinkingLevelMap (mandatory reasoning leaves off unavailable), and a mandatory-reasoning model omits the reasoning field entirely when no effort was requested.

Personalizing the OpenRouter catalog from /models/user keeps only the key models with the key limits and prices, keeps image and classifier entries, and returns the catalog unchanged on 401, 403 or 404.

isContextOverflow matches the HTTP status at the start of the message only (4130 is not 413, 413 in the body is not an overflow) and only for failed responses; isRecoverableLength separates a length stop from a context overflow.
The pi-messages gateway protocol: text and tool-call events, a terminal event requirement (a stream ending without one is an error), and the api being registered as a builtin provider.
Every direct API adapter throws SYNCHRONOUSLY when the api key is missing, instead of returning an error stream.
A 403 whose body carries the real reason must surface both the status and the body, not the SDK opaque 403 status code (no body) message.
The same body-passthrough guarantee per provider tier: openai-completions, openai-responses and Bedrock, with the Bedrock response-stream body never leaking internals.
retryProviderRequest honours retry-after-ms, refuses a server-requested delay above the limit, allows disabling the cap, honours x-should-retry and noRetryStatuses, and aborts the wait.

The builtin provider registry: every provider registers with models, unknown ids return empty results, native constraint metadata is stored, deferred fetch and cancel round-trip, and an unknown provider yields an error stream.
The Qwen Token Plan catalogs expose exactly the documented model sets and send enable_thinking plus reasoning_effort (including xhigh) for the reasoning models.
Radius OAuth: device login straight against the gateway endpoints, refresh without discovery, browser discovery only for the interactive flow, and a failed code exchange rendering a 502 page.
The Radius catalog is replaced wholesale by a refreshed config, a cached catalog can be used with no network, and models disabled by the organization do not reappear from the shipped catalog.

Measures whether replayed Claude thinking actually reaches the provider by comparing reported input tokens with and without the thinking blocks; the Anthropic control passes and the Radius case failed because its done event omits providerThinkingLevel.
getEffortThinkingLevelMap exposes only verified effort values plus none, and refuses to infer thinking-off from an effort list.
Every provider surfaces a responseId on the assistant message.
Retry classification from error MESSAGE text: provider retry guidance, DNS failures, socket drops, HTTP/2 cancellation, service-unavailable wording; plus backoff, abort and onRetryFinished semantics.
Sampling params merge in a defined order: request over model over the effective-thinking-level bucket, with the stream-option keys winning, and ignored entirely by non-OpenAI-compatible APIs.
A hand-written runnable example (not a test) showing the Models API: createModels, setProvider, getAuth, completeSimple and a streaming loop.
The main live provider sweep: text generation, tool calls, streaming, thinking, multi-turn and image input for every provider, plus an Ollama server started and stopped by the suite.
The xhigh and max thinking level matrix per model and provider, including pricing, context window and the compat flags of the newest Claude models.
System prompts are replayable: sections, tool additions and removals collapse into one leading message; a changed tool definition counts as removal plus addition, and non-additive history is flagged.
The telemetry span must survive every request-option surface (direct stream, provider stream, deferred fetch and cancel, image dispatch) and the old telemetryContext name must not compile.
Observing a request must not change the delivered events or the result; the telemetry records token and cost usage but no message content, and a setup failure is reported once.
contentText extracts assistant text blocks and tool-result text, joining with a newline by default and a custom separator on request.
Together model metadata: api, baseUrl, thinkingLevelMap, cost and compat for the Kimi and gpt-oss entries.
Token accounting on abort differs per provider: the OpenAI family and Bedrock report nothing, Kimi reports input only, Anthropic and Google report both, and cost is zero for zero-rate providers.
Live cross-provider handoff proving pipe-separated OpenAI Responses ids are normalized so no provider rejects them as too long (#1022).
A trailing tool call with no result must be filtered so the next request succeeds, and the model may answer or call a new tool.
totalTokens equals input plus output plus cacheRead plus cacheWrite for every provider, including a two-request cache-write then cache-read pair.

Mid-conversation tool load and remove is either a native system message with tool deltas or folded into the prompt for adapters without support, and every request message list starts with the previous one.
Migrating an OpenAI history to Anthropic drops the foreign thoughtSignature and adds a synthetic isError No result provided tool result for trailing orphaned tool calls.
Readable thinking from ANOTHER model is not replayed as text, and only the target model own thinking blocks survive when models alternate (#10995).
The System One classifier maps bool questions to noul, prices usage when the model has a cost, keeps the usage of a billed but unanswered request, and ignores malformed usage.
Emoji and unpaired high surrogates in tool results must not produce no-low-surrogate-in-string JSON errors at any provider.
uuidv7 keeps ids ordered, never lowers the timestamp after a clock rollback, preserves an explicitly given timestamp, uses fresh randomness per tail, and rejects invalid timestamps.

Tool argument validation works when the Function constructor is unavailable, coerces serialized plain JSON schemas with AJV-compatible primitive rules, treats null as omission for optionals, and reports malformed arguments JSON.
The xAI device flow: the exact client id and scope, the poll cadence with slow_down, the refresh expiry margin, and the upstream error code and description on failure.
The xAI Responses request shape and headers, the provider routing, and the User-Agent default with an explicit override on both the Responses and Completions paths.
xhigh works on gpt-5.5 and is a clear error (not a silent downgrade) on a model that does not support it, on both the Responses and Completions APIs.
Xiaomi MiMo drops the deprecated model ids, keeps the replacements, and models reasoning as a plain off/on toggle with no reasoning_effort (#10818).
Live smoke reproducing empty thinking signatures from the Xiaomi AMS endpoint and asserting they survive the replay payload unchanged.
The zai-coding-cn catalog exposes GLM-4.6V with the right api, baseUrl, cost and compat, and Coding Plan models without an API price keep zero cost.
Live smoke over every OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go model in the generated catalog.
Release history 0.99.0 to 1.4.0; records the breaking change that results and close() settle after requesting shutdown, and the #10444/#10283/#10748/#10707/#10631/#10725 fixes.
Example Worker: a Session Durable Object owns the tools while RemoteCodemodeSandbox runs the VM in a separately deployed sandbox Worker; imports /portable so the wasm is not bundled here.
Binds Session and the remote CodemodeSandbox class; the script_name is what puts the scripts in a different isolate.
31-line pointer: two Workers, the local wrangler dev invocation, and deploy the sandbox first because the agent's binding names it.
The whole sandbox Worker: a re-export of CodemodeSandboxDurableObject plus a 404 for HTTP requests.
Sandbox Worker config; cpu_ms 60000 must stay above the interrupt budget so scripts fail with a timeout instead of resetting the Durable Object.
Manifest with six subpath exports, each carrying a source condition pointing at the raw .ts; quickjs-wasi pinned exactly to 3.6.2.
374-line manual: script environment, store, source format, three sandboxes, Cloudflare deployment, model-facing declarations, deterministic runs and the four error kinds.
Ambient declarations for cloudflare:workers and a */quickjs.wasm pattern so the repo needs no Workers types dependency and the files are not published.
Cloudflare entry: re-exports /portable, exposes the Wrangler-compiled wasm, and defines CodemodeSandboxDurableObject with its own interrupt-budget and memory caps.
JSON Schema to TypeScript renderer for the model: 16k char budget, two-stage degradation (drop tags, then unknown), constraint tags, and a 32-expansion cap on $ref.
12-line tool name to JS identifier mapping; invalid characters become _ and the first character must be a letter, _ or $.
Public barrel; re-exports the four output and store limits from the prelude so a host can size its own buffers.
The Node-free entry (inline and remote sandboxes plus the shared base); the worker-thread sandbox stays in the main entry because it needs node:worker_threads.
The host side of every execution: tool table, deadline, abort, bridge decoding; the first terminal event wins and a malformed worker payload becomes a sandbox error rather than an unhandled throw.
Node/Bun launcher: one worker thread and one QuickJS VM per execution; the shared interrupt flag is set before terminate(), and termination is requested without awaiting exit.
In-thread launcher; the interrupt budget of 100k polls is a CPU bound that works while the host's timer and Date.now() are both frozen during synchronous execution.

522-line prelude inside the VM: built-in lockdown with an override carve-out, a tool proxy that names close matches, store size limits, an uncatchable output limit, image signature validation and a stall detector.
Host-to-worker message vocabulary; values cross as JSON strings so the worker never builds structured values itself, and only six message types are accepted.
Remote VM over RPC: the host keeps the tools and call records, output is batched (1000 items / 1 MiB), and the remote caps both the interrupt budget and the memory the client asks for.
Drives one QuickJS VM: deterministic mode (virtual clock, seeded PRNG, UTC, seq-ordered results), the VM fingerprint, and one-job-at-a-time promise draining so await-null loops can be interrupted.
39-line worker entry: starts the VM and relays messages; the host's interrupt flag is read with Atomics and the session is never disposed locally.
Parses the optional first-line @options directive; a misplaced options line is an error rather than silently ignored, and the line is replaced by a blank line to keep line numbers.
Public type surface with the contracts in doc comments: the tool context signal, the four error kinds, run.deliver() ordering, and jsName so a replay cannot rename a tool.
Compiles quickjs.wasm once per path; a failed load is evicted from the cache so the next call retries.
Pins the exact schema-to-TypeScript rendering, including tag order, property sort order and the two-stage budget behaviour.
Runs the deterministic contract against the worker and remote backends and pins the actual PRNG values, the virtual clock and the UTC behaviour.
8-line fake worker that posts a JSON payload taken from the script source, so the host can be fed messages the real prelude never produces.
Runs a real sandbox in a child process and reports the result time and the process-exit time separately, for the Bun non-interruptible-built-in case.
Covers the inline interrupt budget and the remote protocol; asserts that 5000 printed lines need at most 6 exchanges.
869 lines of behaviour run against all three backends, including the escape-hatch, built-in-patch, output-limit and stall-detector cases.
Pins the @options parser, including the rejection of a misplaced options line (#10631) and the blank-line substitution that preserves line numbers.
Pins capacity accounting: admission denial, constructor failure, wasm failure, terminate-without-await, and real Node and Bun process exit.
Build config; files lists the ambient d.ts because exclude does not apply to files.
Vitest config; resolve.conditions ["source"] so the tests import the raw .ts sources through the package's source export.
Release history 1.0.0 to 1.4.0; states the "results match NodeExecutionEnv" contract, the SSH hardening list and the host-key policy.
Exposes the npm version as PI_ENV_VERSION by string-splitting ../package.json, avoiding a JSON dependency in build.rs.

Cargo-generated lockfile (479 lines). I read the header and the first ~35 package blocks and confirmed it is the auto-generated dependency lock pinning the exact = versions from Cargo.toml; I did not read it line by line because it is generated data containing no mechanism.
Rust manifest; every dependency pinned with =, and a release profile of lto, codegen-units=1 and strip because the binary is shipped to remote machines.
Pins Rust 1.96.0 with rustfmt and clippy so the daemon builds identically everywhere.
WHATWG UTF-8 stream decoder matching Node's TextDecoder over chunked input; BOM removal for streams, no BOM handling for byte ranges.
Node-shaped failures: libuv's uv_strerror text table, two-path messages, and extra client fields such as spillPath.

Command execution with streamed output: the per-request Control is registered before the run, abort and kill are different outcomes, output spills to a file past a threshold, and 100 ms of exit grace is collected.
The length-prefixed frame codec; unparseable JSON yields a null value and an error reply rather than desynchronising the stream.
Node-semantics file operations: recursive mkdir's EEXIST and ENOTDIR rules, rm's ERR_FS_EISDIR, and lstat under the decoded name so non-UTF-8 names report ENOENT as Node does.
gitignore-aware tree listing via the ignore crate (the one fd and ripgrep use); records are a kind byte, the relative path and a NUL, bounded by entries, bytes and timeout.

The daemon: frame loop, a 16-worker file pool, dedicated threads for exec/watch/pty, per-handle serialised chunk writes, control replies ahead of bulk output, and kill-everything when the client goes silent.
The single stdout writer with two queues; control frames always precede bulk output and unsent bulk above 4 MiB blocks the reader, as a full pipe would.
Pseudo-terminal support: openpty, a session leader with the pty as controlling terminal, SIGWINCH on resize, foreground process-group reporting and ENOTSUP on Windows.
Port of Durable's LineScanner: locates a line range and measures its decoded UTF-8 size, and the result is independent of the chunk size.
The OS seam; the Synthetic error lets the daemon report libuv codes the operating system did not produce.
Unix half: errno to libuv names, O_NONBLOCK and O_NOFOLLOW readers, Node's shell resolution, setsid with default signals in pre_exec, group kill and 128+signal exit codes.
Windows half: a hand-written Win32-to-libuv error map, CreateFileW dispositions, libuv's quote_cmd_arg, a sorted child environment, a Job Object for tree kill and the file index for identity.
Port of NodeFileWatcher: native events only trigger a debounced rescan, unreliable filesystems force polling, and running out of watchers reports overflow.

The output window: only a prefix whose remainder still proves exclusion is dropped, the cut lands on a character boundary, and the skip is reported as byte and line counts while the tail is still delivered.
The normative wire protocol: frames, the PI-ENV sync marker, cancellation, scheduling fairness, liveness and every operation including hello.features.
Which side does what (the client owns paths, aborts, errors and read chunking; the daemon owns syscalls, processes, spill and line scans) and the rules the standard libraries do not follow.
Manifest; the published package ships the daemon binaries in bin/ and the docs, and its version is the one the Rust build reports.
66 lines: the SSH hardening list, the lazy-versus-eager connect choice, listFiles' not_supported fallback and the supported platform matrix.

The framed client: the PI-ENV sync marker, strict frame validation that tears the connection down, plain Uint8Array payload copies, and a failed start that is not remembered so the next request retries.
Maps the daemon's Node-style codes to Durable's FileError codes and provides abortResult.
Public barrel; it also exports the SSH bootstrap primitives deployDaemon, detectPlatform and sshArguments.
listFiles over the wire with a pre-request hello.features check, plus LocalExecutionEnv so local and remote environments list files with the same code.

957 lines reproducing NodeExecutionEnv remotely: path resolution including Windows drive-relative paths, abort checkpoints, 8-deep parallel reads, 512 KiB writes, byte-order directory sort and the exec error kinds.
The SSH bootstrap: a fixed hardened argument list, content-addressed daemon deployment verified by SHA-256, host keys never replaced silently, and atomic one-at-a-time known-hosts rewrites.
Remote terminal client: the pty request is the terminal's lifetime, input is chunked at 1 MiB, foreground jobs are reported, and errors after the start are carried by `exited`.
Remote watcher with 1s to 30s backoff reconnect that reports overflow because changes during the outage were not seen.
Runs Durable's shared env conformance suite against both RemoteExecutionEnv and LocalExecutionEnv.
Locates the daemon binary (PI_ENV_DAEMON else the cargo debug build) and throws a clear build instruction at import time.
Differential test: 60 seeds times 25 random operations run against NodeExecutionEnv and RemoteExecutionEnv, compared after normalising the root and keeping only the error code.
A dependency-free Node stand-in for a daemon released before hello.features: it answers hello without features and refuses every other operation.
Output-window arithmetic, twenty abort attempts, the not_supported path, a killed daemon's stale handle, and a 3.5 MB chunked write and read round trip.
The conformance suite over a real SSH server configured by CI environment variables, with every stage logged so a hang shows where it is.
Drives a disposable real sshd: key trust, content-addressed deployment, tampered-daemon replacement, lazy connect and the host-key change policy.
Remote terminal behaviour: raw bytes (0xff survives), resize, exit code, foreground job detection, ordering of 4000 writes and kill on close.
Build config with paths mapping chord and pi-durable to their built dist type declarations.
Vitest config with the source resolve condition; unlike codemode and mcp it does not enable globals.
Release history; records the transport signal fix (#10598), the aborted-refresh fix (#10565) and the OAuth response-shape fixes.
The MIT licence of the Anthropic MCP TypeScript SDK, shipped because src/oauth/* is adapted from it and the package is published.
Manifest; the only runtime dependency is cross-spawn, and there are three entries (root, /oauth and /testing).
136 lines; states the transport-owns-framing and client-owns-correlation rule, the provider limits when wrapping MCP tools, and what is out of scope.
The three-member token-provider contract, including the rule that closing a session reuses the last request's token instead of asking the provider.

The single place pi writes output files; mode 0600 and the wx flag ("never follows a link someone else placed at the path"), currently in the OS temp directory.

Path canonicalisation, normalisation and containment; getCwdRelativePath is the single is-inside-this-root predicate reused by the managed install, the quarantine and the config selector, and getFileRevision stamps dev:ino:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs.

Lazy, failure-tolerant wrapper around the Photon WASM library; fs.readFileSync is patched for the duration of the import to redirect a missing photon_rs_bg.wasm read to a fallback next to the executable, then restored.
One-line helper returning pi's detailed User-Agent for its own network requests.

Shell and PowerShell discovery, the shell environment, binary-output sanitisation (including the U+FFF9-FFFB interlinear characters that crash string-width) and tracked detached children killed on parent signals.
One-line abort-aware sleep that rejects with "Aborted" when the signal fires.

22 languages registered eagerly and the rest loaded lazily in a setImmediate after the first frame; highlight.js's HTML is parsed into a scope stack and themed here, so no span markup reaches the terminal.
BOM handling: splitBom returns the BOM separately, stripBom removes it; used by the theme loader, the changelog reader and the package manager.

Normalises image blocks produced by tools (extensions, MCP bridges) before they enter history, because an oversized image makes the provider reject the whole conversation; a conversion failure keeps the original block rather than deleting the tool's output.

Ensures fd and rg exist, downloading from GitHub releases; the latest version is resolved from the release-page redirect rather than the rate-limited API, extraction tries tar/unzip/PowerShell in order and lists every attempt, and the extract dir is unique per download because startup downloads run concurrently.

The "is there a newer pi?" check; formatVersionCheckError unwraps Node's generic "fetch failed" to the errno codes, isNewerPackageVersion degrades to a string compare for non-semver tags, and PI_OFFLINE / PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK short-circuit it.

Works around Windows locking a loaded .node file: reads process.report's sharedObjects, renames each loaded addon into a quarantine dir under node_modules and copies it back so the path exists but is unlocked.
Detects WSL from WSL_DISTRO_NAME/WSLENV and by grepping /proc/version, so it also works in a container with neither set.
Writes the small classic ZIP archives used by bug reports with no dependency, assembling the local headers, central directory and EOCD by hand over zlib.deflateRawSync and zlib.crc32.

Auto-compaction: overflow recovery fires at most once (runAutoCompaction called once, compaction_end carries a "failed after one compact-and-retry attempt" message); threshold compaction for an ERROR message fires only from a POST-compaction successful assistant usage, and stale pre-compaction usage is ignored.

Forking: a fork from a user message yields an empty new session whose session FILE does not exist on disk yet; --no-session forks stay in memory (sessionFile undefined); forking mid-conversation keeps the prefix.

E2E compaction against a real LLM: manual compact() emits compaction_start/compaction_end (reason "manual", aborted false, willRetry false), persists exactly one compaction entry with summary/firstKeptEntryId/tokensBefore, and works in --no-session mode.

Concurrent-prompt guard: prompt() while streaming REJECTS with a message naming steer/followUp; steer()/followUp() resolve to "queued"; extension-sourced steering is delivered with source "extension"; a tool_call extension event fires only after the queued agent events are persisted, and a slow message_end handler does not reorder persistence.

An extension may registerProvider (override object or a native pi-ai Provider) at load time, at session_start or at command time; the ACTIVE model's baseUrl changes with no reload, verified by capturing the model inside streamFunction.

Dynamic tool registration: the bash spawn hook sees PI_SESSION_ID/PI_SESSION_FILE/PI_PROVIDER/PI_MODEL/PI_REASONING_LEVEL (opt-out via exposeSessionEnvironment:false), the tool registry refreshes after a late registration, every tool carries sourceInfo (builtin/inline/sdk), and a tool with no promptSnippet stays ACTIVE but is unadvertised in the prompt.

Auto-retry: auto_retry_start/auto_retry_end events with attempt numbers, the agent delay is capped (1,2,4,5), network_error is retried, and prompt() must wait for the FULL tool loop after a successful retry rather than unblocking on the first message_end.

Session lifecycle: session_before_switch/session_shutdown/session_start ordering for new/resume/fork, cancellation leaves the session untouched, and a CAPTURED extension ctx THROWS an actionable message ("this extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload...") once the session is replaced.

getSessionStats separates CUMULATIVE token/cost totals (covering compacted-away history) from CURRENT context usage, reports context as null right after a compaction, uses post-compaction usage rather than stale kept usage, and groups tool/summary usage apart from model-attributed usage.

Tree navigation with branch summarization: the summary attaches to the SELECTED node's parent (a1), abort during summarization leaves entries and leaf unchanged, navigating to a root user message empties the conversation, and custom instructions are appended as "Additional focus".

stripAnsi is fuzzed against a chalk-compatible reference regex over 248 generated escape inputs and throws the same TypeError message as chalk on non-strings; RIS and single-byte ESC sequences are stripped without leaking the final byte.

CLI arg parsing: every flag and shorthand has a test, an invalid enum value produces a structured diagnostic instead of a throw, a flag NEVER consumes the next option as its value, unknown long flags are captured into an unknownFlags map, and tool modifiers are +name/-name exact names only (patterns rejected).

AssistantMessageComponent: OSC 133 zone markers only for tool-call-free messages, adjacent thinking blocks coalesce into one hidden label and collapse individually on click, and Markdown transformers chain in registration order, re-run on width change, and CONTINUE PAST a throw without mutating the source message.

`pi auth check`: a configured provider is "ready", an unresolved $ENV reference is credentials_not_configured, malformed auth.json is "invalid", an unknown provider is provider_not_found, OAuth refresh is opt-in, and the check never creates the auth file OR its parent directory.

Credential store: $ENV and !command resolution, per-credential env scopes, THREE concurrent readers across two instances take exactly ONE lock, 0600 file modes, Windows EPERM lock retries are bounded to 6 and only on win32, a compromised lock is surfaced, a malformed auth.json is never overwritten, and an aborted mutation is never committed.
Login dialog and MCP sign-in screen copy the auth URL on ctrl+x and report "Copied URL to clipboard"; the key is ignored when there is no auth URL.
Windows-only: executeBashWithOperations and the bash tool resolve once the shell exits even when a detached grandchild still holds the inherited stdio pipe (the child is taskkill'ed in cleanup).
BashExecutionComponent's collapsed output is re-wrapped at RENDER time, not construction time (regression #2569): every rendered line's visibleWidth stays within the render-time width after a resize.

The blockImages setting is a DISPLAY-layer filter: the read tool and processFileArguments always return image content, and a BMP on disk is converted to a PNG attachment with a "[Image converted from image/bmp to image/png.]" marker line.

Branch summarization never overrides tool choice, REJECTS a tool call ("Branch summarization attempted to call a tool") and rejects a length-capped summary ("generation hit the token cap and the summary is incomplete") rather than returning a partial one.

An extension can supply the branch summary via session_before_tree; the summary entry is stored with fromHook:true and fromId pointing at the abandoned source, and its usage lands in the session totals.

Bug-report flow preserves pasted line breaks through the editor/selector steps, and redaction strips URL credentials and secret query params (encoded as %3Credacted%3E) and redacts secret-looking JSON KEYS while keeping token COUNTS.

constrainedSampling is a provider-side conversion, not a schema change (the execution schema's required list is unchanged); wrapToolDefinition preserves an explicit opt-out and the definition's execute/render/promptGuidelines identity, and an extension re-registering a tool without strict sampling leaves the system prompt byte-identical.

computeCacheWaste prices a prompt-cache miss as (write price - read price) x missed tokens (105k at $3.75-$0.30/M = $0.36225), SKIPS the turn after a compaction reset, counts a model switch as a miss, and detectCacheMiss reports the idle time since the last request as the cause.

CacheWarmer: warm only when expected savings beat the warm cost (missCost 0.575 vs warmCost 0.050), an extension may force or veto (recorded as the note "extension override"), the safe deadline is re-checked AFTER an async extension decision, a replaced request is aborted, and a failed refresh records no usage.
normalizeChangelogLinks rewrites package-relative doc links to tag-pinned GitHub blob/tree URLs, canonicalizes the old pi-mono repository URLs, and leaves external and local-anchor links untouched.
createChatViewport defaults the transcript scrollbar to "auto" and accepts a "hidden" override.

runClipboardCommand preserves binary output, distinguishes empty success from failure, times out WITHOUT blocking the event loop, runs outside pi's own process group (so Ctrl+Z cannot suspend the daemon), and rejects output above the buffer limit.
WSL2/WSLg clipboard often yields image/bmp; readClipboardImage converts BOTH the command BMP and the native BMP to PNG (PNG magic bytes) on linux and win32.
A native clipboard image error aborts the paste entirely: no text read, no editor change, no render request, exactly one error message.

readClipboardImage probes Wayland then X11 then native, STOPS the fallback on an empty result, refuses to probe image types the clipboard does not advertise, tries PowerShell before a broken native X11 bridge on WSL, and PROPAGATES a native transfer error instead of falling through.

Pasted file paths take precedence over their icon image, paths containing terminal control characters are rejected, and in bash mode paths are SHELL-QUOTED (a path containing $(touch hacked) is quoted, not executed).

Clipboard text copy across macOS/Linux (wl-paste/xclip/xsel)/Termux/WSL: the native write is awaited before OSC 52, a local Linux failure THROWS rather than reporting an unverified OSC 52 write as success, oversized OSC 52 payloads are refused, and WSL uses PowerShell only when OSC 52 is unavailable or oversized.

Codemode renderer: hides the script header, prices each model call and the total, caps collapsed output by WRAPPED lines (not logical lines), and shows "Elapsed 3.0s" while running but "Took 5.1s" once settled.

Worker admission: at capacity a script WAITS rather than failing, capacity is released on actual worker EXIT (not on the result), a launch that resumes after a timeout starts no worker, an abort while waiting says "The script did not start.", and an invalid PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS=0 is ignored.
resolveCodemodeWorkerSpecifier picks a different worker entrypoint per packaging (bun-binary relative source / bundled-node emitted sibling / unbundled undefined).
Compaction summary, branch summary and skill invocation components all toggle open/closed when their marker row is clicked.

The extensions.md compaction example is imported and EXECUTED so the documented API cannot drift from the code; the example routes the summary through modelRegistry.complete WITHOUT an apiKey option (the credential comes from the registry).

Compaction extension contract: session_before_compact may cancel ("Compaction cancelled") or supply the whole compaction, a THROWING extension is ignored and the default compaction runs (fromExtension:false), and all before-handlers run before all after-handlers.
Compaction file-op accounting reads nested tool calls recorded on a tool result, so a codemode script's read/edit are attributed to the right files (and a write is not).
serializeConversation truncates tool results to 2000 chars with an explicit "[... 3000 more characters truncated]" marker, never truncates user/assistant text, and OMITS thinking blocks entirely.

Summarizer options: the reasoning level is honoured only for reasoning models, every summarization uses a FRESH routing session with cacheRetention forced to "none", tool calls and length-capped summaries are REJECTED rather than degraded, a split turn keeps the previous summary, and the prompt uses clear "# Conversation" / "# Instructions" boundaries so a summarized transcript is not read as a fresh user ask.

Compaction core: context tokens are estimated from the LAST non-zero non-aborted assistant usage plus a trailing estimate, findCutPoint never cuts inside a tool result and falls back to the latest valid cut point (regression #9740), a system message is NOT conversation history, buildSessionContext honours only the latest compaction, and a re-compaction that would not move the window is skipped.

The four generated JSON Schemas are compared BYTE-FOR-BYTE against the committed artifacts ("is stale; run npm run generate:schemas") and compiled to check that the values the runtime accessors accept and reject are the values the schema accepts and rejects.

Config value migrations leave uppercase-looking API key/header values alone, never throw or rewrite a malformed models.json (the parse error names the file), and the registry still resolves the literal key afterwards.

Install-method detection and self-update for npm/pnpm/yarn/bun: an unknown wrapper install and a non-writable prefix REFUSE to self-update, a renamed package updates in two steps, and a deleted pnpm install reports {kind: "removed"} instead of reading a package.json further up.

Crash attribution matches stack frames beneath a loaded extension root, normalises Windows paths, dedupes two entries of the same package, and does NOT attribute a sibling single-file package or a path mentioned only in the error message.

Credential printing: --model without --provider resolves only among CATALOG models of configured providers, an expired OAuth token is refreshed before printing, and an unknown auth option is reported with a usage hint and exit code 1.
An explicit editor history binding takes precedence over the default model-cycling binding.
CustomMessageComponent passes and updates outputPad in the MessageRenderOptions given to an extension renderer.

Tool loadout: defaultTools selects the active set, +name/-name modifiers apply to it, a reload only activates NEWLY added tools, and the loadout is RECORDED IN THE TRANSCRIPT (a system message with toolsAdded/toolsRemoved) and restored PER BRANCH on resume and on tree navigation.

Docs gate: every page must be reachable from docs.json navigation (a graph traversal from the nav root), no broken local markdown links, no duplicate public slugs, no orphaned pages; links are harvested with marked's lexer.

prepareArguments folds legacy top-level oldText/newText into edits while the legacy fields stay OUT of the advertised schema, a JSON-string `edits` is parsed, and non-object input passes through untouched.

A large edit diff renders in the call preview and the settled result does NOT force a full terminal clear (fullRedraws and clear counts unchanged), the preview is reconstructible from a settled result alone, and a preflight error renders no diff.
areExperimentalFeaturesEnabled is true only when PI_EXPERIMENTAL is exactly "1" ("0" and "true" are off).

The exported HTML viewer renders emphasis next to CJK punctuation while keeping CommonMark flanking rules for non-CJK text; the viewer script is executed in a node:vm sandbox so the real marked build is under test.
The HTML export strips the Pi-generated <skill> wrapper, renders the skill body as markdown, and emits the skill invocation and the user message as SIBLING blocks matching the TUI layout.
Export CSS preserves whitespace only on output line elements, not on the container; ANSI lines are emitted without source whitespace and TUI padding lines are trimmed.

Export sanitization: a scheme allow-list for markdown link/image hrefs, C0 controls stripped before the check, and escapeHtml on href, mimeType, image data, entry ids and every session field rendered via innerHTML.
The share export appends a custom "pi.share" entry carrying the systemPrompt and tool definitions, keeps conversation ids and parent links intact, and re-imports as a valid session.

Extension discovery: direct .ts/.js files, one-level subdirectories with index.ts or a package.json "pi.extensions" list (which beats index.ts), tilde-relative package paths, no recursion past one level, and an extension importing the host package is still LOCAL (regression #9863).

The "input" extension event contract: continue / transform / handled, transforms CHAIN across handlers, "handled" short-circuits the rest, the source and streamingBehavior are passed through, and a THROWING handler is caught and the input continues.

ExtensionRunner: the reserved shortcut set is computed from the CURRENT keybindings, tool name collisions keep the FIRST while command collisions are suffixed :1/:2, a tool without a parameter schema REJECTS the whole extension, the user_bash hook FAILS CLOSED on any invalid handler result, boundary proposals chain and a later handler may repair an invalid one, tool_result patches MERGE rather than replace, provider registration is queued pre-bind, and the event-subscription contract during dispatch is pinned precisely.
External editing happens in a private 0700 temp directory removed afterwards; a failed editor keeps the original content; an emptied prompt returns empty content.

withFileMutationQueue serialises mutations per REAL PATH (a symlink alias shares the same queue) while different files run in parallel, and an aborted write/edit keeps the queue locked until the in-flight write actually settles.
A forked package name suppresses first-time setup even with PI_EXPERIMENTAL=1.
First-time setup needs experimental on AND the default agent dir AND no settings.json; analytics default to off and the tracking id is minted only on opt-in and kept across toggles.

33-line JSON fixture: one assistant message with a thinking block (a long thinking string plus a long thinkingSignature, both single-line and shown truncated to 2000 chars by the reader) and a text block carrying a real model reasoning trace, with usage/cost fields.

2.37 MB captured real pi session log (1,003 JSONL records: 1 v1 header, 990 messages, 2 compaction, 5 model_change, 5 thinking_level_change) - not read line by line because the bulk is embedded file contents; parsed every line for a record/role/tool census, read both compaction summaries in full (4,291 and 3,649 chars), resolved both firstKeptEntryIndex targets (293, 551) to their user messages, read the 3 bashExecution entries (one truncated=true with fullOutputPath), read the head/tail records, and confirmed no credential material.

0-byte .gitkeep whose DIRECTORY is the fixture: skills.test.ts:349 passes it as loadSkills' agentDir so the <agentDir>/skills default layer (skills.ts:458) resolves to zero skills; exists because git does not track empty dirs.

0-byte .gitkeep whose DIRECTORY is the fixture: skills.test.ts:350 passes it as loadSkills' cwd so the <cwd>/.pi/skills project layer (skills.ts:459, CONFIG_DIR_NAME=".pi") resolves to zero skills, isolating the loader from the repo checkout too.

25-line fake $EDITOR spawned by editInExternalEditor: writes a capture JSON (filePath, content, dir entries, dir mode & 0o777) BEFORE honouring --fail, then exits 1 or writes "edited\n"/"" so external-editor.test.ts can assert what the editor saw, the 0700 scratch dir, and cleanup-on-failure.

Generated capture of a real 1019-line session transcript (session header + message envelopes with provider/model/usage/stopReason); sampled head and tail and the entry shapes rather than read line by line, because it is recorded data with no logic in it.
Minimal valid skill named "calendar" ("First calendar skill."); the first of a colliding pair used to pin name-collision precedence.
Second skill also named "calendar" ("Second calendar skill."); exists only to collide with the first by name.
Frontmatter name "bad--name" pins that consecutive hyphens are accepted (only the character set and 64-char length are validated).
Carries the non-standard frontmatter field "disable-model-invocation: true", the flag that keeps a skill out of model-initiated invocation.
Name "Invalid_Name" (uppercase + underscore) pins that an invalid name is a warning, not a rejection - the skill still loads.
Frontmatter "description: [unclosed bracket" pins that unparseable YAML is skipped with a diagnostic instead of crashing the loader.
A 96-character name pins the 64-character skill-name limit as a warning while the skill still loads.
Frontmatter with name but no description - the one fixture where the skill is NOT loaded, because the description is the model's only trigger.
| block scalar description spanning three lines pins that multiline descriptions are normalised to a single line for the prompt.
Directory "name-mismatch" vs frontmatter name "different-name" pins that the frontmatter name wins and the directory name is irrelevant.
A skill one directory deep pins that skills are discovered recursively.
Markdown with no --- block at all pins that a non-skill file in the skills tree is ignored rather than reported as an error.
Nested skill with a description but no name pins that a nameless nested skill loses to the root skill.
Root skill with a description but no name pins that the root skill is preferred over a nested one.
Frontmatter carrying author/version pins that unknown frontmatter keys are ignored without a diagnostic.
Canonical valid skill used as the positive control for the loader.

Footer's git-branch detection: mocks child_process, hand-builds a reftable worktree (.git/worktrees/src/HEAD + commondir + reftable/tables.list), and pins the 5000ms watcher-error recovery that re-creates the FSWatcher.

Footer layout: fake AgentSession aggregating usage across message/branch_summary/compaction/tool-result entries; pins the home-prefix rule (a sibling of $HOME is not abbreviated), display-width budgeting with Hangul text, and the "(sub)" marker reserved for a declared subscription.

Pins the printed resume command: POSIX single-quote escaping of the session dir, the dir only shown for a non-default dir, and four distinct undefined returns (non-TTY, in-memory, missing file, unset file).
Frontmatter parser: CRLF normalisation, YAML block scalars, invalid YAML throws with a position, and an unterminated --- block treated as prose rather than an error.

Pins the git-merge-and-resolve example extension: agent_end handler, conflict list from git diff --diff-filter=U, conflicts re-sent as a USER message, no fetch/merge when a merge is already in progress, and skips for non-repo/no-upstream/no-conflicts.
Pins parseGitUrl: protocol URLs accepted bare, shorthand only behind the "git:" prefix, and a list of unsafe install paths (traversal, %2F, absolute, backslash, NUL) that must return null.

Pins git-backed extension updates: the forced refspec "+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main" with --prune --no-tags for force-push remotes, and the requirement that the source carries the "git:" prefix.

Pins proxy handling: settings never override an existing HTTP(S)_PROXY, a real CONNECT tunnel asserted via the proxy request line, and a 2s autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout applied without changing Node's global default.
Pins magic-byte mime detection (GIF87a/GIF89a/BMP) and that BMP->PNG conversion happens BEFORE auto-resize, with the conversion reported as a user-visible hint.
Pins the Photon resize/convert helpers: formatDimensionNote returns undefined when the image was not resized, and otherwise reports original size, displayed size and scale factor.

Pins every resize caller: when a safe image cannot be produced the read tool returns a text "Image omitted" result and the file processor emits zero attachments; the model's own inputLimits.images.resize profile is forwarded.
Pins first-prompt assembly: stdin + file text + the first CLI message are merged into one prompt and the first CLI message is consumed out of parsed.messages.
Pins the input-transform-streaming extension: a "steer" skips the exec entirely, a "followUp" runs it, and a failed/empty transform falls back to action "continue".

Pins the one-time Anthropic subscription warning: shown once, getAuth called at most once, an already-known OAuth credential skips getAuth entirely, and the anthropicExtraUsage setting suppresses all lookups.
Pins the "Anthropic dropped N thinking blocks" notice: gated by the cache-miss-notice setting, count-only in the chat, and suppressed when the same diagnostic already exists in the session branch.

Pins when a bug report is suggested: an allow-list of retryable failures (5xx, 429, overloaded, network lost, timeout) and cancellations suppress it; an install-change error shows the install warning instead; a crash frame names the extension and pi -ne.
Pins /clone: forks at the leaf with position "at", clears the editor, shows "Cloned to new session", and reports "Nothing to clone yet" when there is no leaf.

Pins compaction in the TUI: the cost notice renders after its summary, compaction vs branch summary are labelled differently, notices obey the cache-miss setting, and flushCompactionQueue re-sends queued messages as a steer.

Pins extension dialog stacking (#11166, #9909): a second dialog stacks over the first and answering it restores the first, an AbortSignal removes a hidden dialog, a confirm opened from a custom component stacks above it, and focus returns to the editor when the stack empties.

Pins /import and /export argument parsing: quotes stripped, apostrophes preserved in unquoted paths, token boundaries enforced (/important is not /import), and a missing file reported as a non-fatal error.

Pins startup races: a submit during startup is restored with "Startup is still in progress", a submit before the input callback exists is queued in pendingUserInputs and drained first by getUserInput, and the text is never dropped.

Biggest UI test in the shard (1372 lines): status-line coalescing for immediately-sequential messages, the compact startup resource listing grouped by SourceInfo scope/origin across local, npm, scoped-npm, git and CLI extensions, and the quiet-startup header/details modes.

Pins Ctrl+Z suspend: on Windows it is refused outright with no signal handlers or timers registered; elsewhere SIGTSTP/SIGCONT plus a 2^30ms keep-alive restore the TUI, and a failed suspend still cleans up its handlers.

Pins tree navigation: availability is re-checked AFTER the abort settles (#9178/#9179), a busy rejection leaves the active operation's UI completely untouched, and navigation is allowed once compaction finishes.

Pins the TUI shell: the alternate screen is entered only in fullscreen mode (asserted on the exact \x1b[?1049h sequence), the jump-to-bottom hint uses the configured keybinding, and the status indicators/clipboard are exercised through a recording virtual terminal.

Pins the jev-router example: a classifier model's complexity probability selects the model per phase, the switch happens mid-turn (sol, sol, luna, luna), and the phase is persisted as a virtual-model-state custom entry.
Pins the keybinding-name migration: old names map to namespaced ids, the new name wins when both exist, and old names still load in memory before the file is rewritten.
Pins platform keybinding defaults: WSL is detected via WSL_DISTRO_NAME or WSL_INTEROP but NOT WT_SESSION alone, and the seven bindings that differ between the Windows and Unix families.

Pins the built-in llama.cpp extension: only loaded and sleeping models are exposed, contextWindow/maxTokens/input come from the server's own meta and architecture, chat-template thinking support is discovered from /v1/props (#9528), and a non-http server URL is rejected.

Pins fetchWithRetry: the timeout budget is shared across attempts (the same AbortSignal object), a per-attempt timeout gets its own controller, an already-aborted caller signal rejects without calling fetch, and transient 503s are retried.
Pins the "max" thinking level: accepted by the CLI and by settings, and a legacy theme without colors.thinkingMax falls back to the xhigh border colour.

Pins the pi mcp CLI: list exits non-zero if anything at all is wrong (spawn failure or invalid entry), per-server state/tool-count/exposure/scope, --json output, add/remove scoping, and friendly errors for unknown servers and non-OAuth logout.
Committed expected results per protocol version and scenario (passing/failing check ids), including the synthetic "pi-client" check and the keyword-level JSON-Schema preservation checks.

The client under test: drives pi's real McpServerConnection/signInMcpServer, simulates a browser that approves the OAuth URL without following the redirect and delivers it to pi's loopback callback, and caps simulated sign-ins at three.

Documents the upstream MCP conformance harness, the three ways a run fails, the rule that newly-passing checks are reported, and the three known failures (elicitation, basic CIMD, scope-retry-limit) plus the excluded 2026-07-28 protocol.

The runner: pinned upstream package, three protocol modes, detached children killed as a process group on timeout, npm_config_ignore_scripts for the npx fetch, INFO/SKIPPED statuses ignored, and a hard error when the baseline was made for another suite version.

Biggest MCP test (868 lines): config merge (project override needs trust), disabled servers kept so /mcp can re-enable them, a dropped connection degrades to "disconnected" and reconnects on the next call, 503 is retried but 400 fails permanently, tool calls are not retried while resource reads are, close() stops pending retries (#10249), and the prompt section is capped with a "find their tools with searchTools()" tail.
Pins the MCP manager status screen: the cancel affordance is rendered only for operations that can be cancelled (#10565) and the word "cancel" is absent otherwise.

Pins MCP OAuth: a single-flight refresh across three processes sharing a credential store and lock dir (the server rotates refresh tokens, so only one refresh may run), the others wait via provider.settled(), the lock is released, paste-sign-in validates the redirect URI, and CIMD failure registers nothing.

Pins credential keying: tokens are keyed by server name AND url so two servers sharing a SERVER_URL stay separate (#10252), and legacy url-keyed state migrates lazily to the first server that loads it (-/_ are the same server).

Pins the Mermaid renderer: streaming vs settled rendering differ on purpose, a parse failure falls back to the code block with a warning, multiple partial-render warnings are summarised as "(+1 more)", and an oversized diagram is left untouched.

Pins the catalog negotiation (#9099): types=chat,image,classifier plus pi-version, the newest catalog revision the client satisfies, the legacy fallback for revisions predating typed shards, and the fact that the negotiated revision decides the final provider URL (/api/v1/messages vs /api/v1/chat/completions).

Pins the interactive catalog refresh: concurrent callers share ONE runtime refresh, one caller aborting rejects only that caller and leaves the shared signal alive, and a refresh with no waiters left is aborted so a later one can start.

Biggest provider test (2146 lines): models.json baseUrl vs models[] semantics, per-model overrides that deep-merge compat and are ignored for unknown ids, and apiKey resolution via literal, $ENV, ${ENV}, $$ escaping and !command (trimmed stdout; failure/nonexistent/empty all yield undefined).

Pins model selection: an ambiguous provider/model id is reported with both qualified names rather than resolved by catalog order, a stored credential may disambiguate but --api-key may not, the :thinking suffix is stripped in the fallback path, and no double-prefixing of provider/.

Pins the provider-owned auth surface: availability reads are scoped to the provider asked for, a read failure is recorded in runtime.getError(), and an extension-registered OAuth provider projects into the login options with its own method name and isSubscription flag.

Pins the classifier model kind: a classifier is invisible to the chat-model lookup, auth is resolved at runtime, and the per-provider image encoding (image_url vs assets) compat applies to classifier models exactly as to chat models.

Pins the Cloudflare gateway compat endpoint: cf-aig-authorization is used and neither Authorization nor x-api-key is sent, and both the ModelRuntime path and the ModelRegistry path materialise the identical URL.

Pins credential/availability ordering: the availability snapshot is published before login/logout resolve, same-provider operations are serialised, and a failed post-login catalog refresh raises CredentialSynchronizationError while the credential STAYS stored.

Pins the image model kind: image models are listed separately from chat models, an extension's model list replaces the undeclared models of every operation, and a chat-only provider does not gain image/classification through a headers override.

Pins the extension-provider lifecycle: native providers with their own auth implementation (and a resolve() that may change the baseUrl), a native provider with a stored credential marked configured at registration (#9962), and modifyModels extending the list by credential with logout removing exactly those models.
Shared helper building a ModelRegistry over a ModelRuntime; uses an in-memory models store so unit tests never take a file-backed catalog lock, and allowModelNetwork: false.

Pins the model picker: the current model stays check-marked while browsing (cursor arrow is a separate mark), the save hint uses the configured keybinding, and a failed catalog refresh reports the count of failed catalogs with the cached models.

Pins the file-backed catalog store: concurrent readers across two store instances take the lock once and share the reload, an aborting reader does not cancel the shared reload for the other, a write cancelled while waiting for the lock must not write afterwards, and the file mode is preserved.

Pins nested tool calls: hierarchical child ids (call/1), events carrying the parent id, the record taken once, and NESTED_CALL_LIMITS capping call count, error chars and a 32 KiB total-argument budget with unfinished calls marked status "unfinished" and complete:false.

Pins the login picker: options are projected from provider-owned auth methods with no provider-specific filtering, and the credential source is shown verbatim (env:, key in models.json, command in models.json, subscription configured, or not configured).

Pins the one-space output pad across five component shapes (bash, tool execution with and without a definition, self-rendered edit result, compaction summary) by comparing the rendered lines at pad 0 and pad 1.

Pins pi install/update/config: the managed-install release layout, the three-state package override cycle (enabled / -disabled / inherited-removed), built-in extension toggles with the builtin: prefix, and "Did you mean npm:pi-formatter?" style errors.
Pins the npm entry points: the executable uses the bundle (dist/bundle/cli.js) while the library import and the rpc-entry are separate modular artefacts.
Pins git source parsing and identity: getPackageIdentity normalises the git:-prefixed, https:// and ssh:// spellings to one key, and without the prefix the shorthands are classified as local.

Biggest file in the shard (2862 lines): install/update/resolve for npm, git and local sources; a failed clone or dependency install removes the directory it created, an existing git checkout is reconciled (fetch + reset --hard FETCH_HEAD^{commit} + clean -fdx), package.json pi.extensions manifests are honoured in subdirectories, updates are batched per scope and run in parallel, PI_OFFLINE skips installs/refreshes/checks, legacy global npm installs migrate into the managed root, and runCommandCapture resolves only on close.

Pins the tool-facing path helpers: ~ expands only as home or ~/..., a tilde-prefixed filename stays literal (with @ stripped), NBSP normalises, and resolveReadPath recovers the macOS filename mismatches (NFC/NFD, curly vs straight quotes, U+202F before AM/PM, lowercase am/pm).

Pins the path utilities: canonicalizePath resolves symlinks but falls back to the raw path, getCwdRelativePath rejects ../ but keeps ..config, resolvePath accepts file:// URLs but rejects a Windows file-URL pathname on Windows, and normalizeWindowsShellPath translates /c, /cygdrive and /mnt drive paths.
Pins the User-Agent format pi/<version> (<platform>; <runtime>; <arch>) with bun/<v> when running under Bun.

Pins the plan-mode example: toggling preserves the user's custom tools, a response with no plan prompts nothing, refinement is queued as a follow-up USER message and execution as a follow-up custom message with triggerTurn.

Pins the plan-mode helpers: isSafeCommand is an allow-list of read-only commands (not a denylist), refusals include redirects, sudo, editors and installs, and the todo extraction/completion markers are normalised.

Pins the PowerShell discovery order (pwsh on PATH, pwsh under ProgramFiles, powershell on PATH, powershell under SystemRoot) without assuming a drive letter or Windows directory name (#9490), and a clear error when nothing is found.
Pins the PowerShell tool: the process-local ExecutionPolicy Bypass (asserted via Get-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process) and UTF-8 output surviving the round trip.

Pins the headless mode: session_shutdown is emitted on every path (success, error, truncated), a length-truncated answer warns on stderr and exits non-zero (#10799), and json mode prompts without images.

Pins the terminal program status: only the OUTCOME of a run is reported (a retried error then success is done, only the final error is error with the first line only, an abort is idle), the status never carries model output, a failed recovery compaction is the run's error unless a later response succeeds, and blocked dialogs are tracked per source.

Pins prompt-template parsing and substitution: $1/$2/$@/$ARGUMENTS, NO recursive substitution of patterns inside argument values, out-of-range placeholders become empty, and an invalid frontmatter file becomes a warning diagnostic while valid templates load.

Pins the Radius provider: a legacy credential with a gatewayConfig restores its catalog with no network at all, catalog refresh is opt-in via allowModelNetwork, no auth means no model and no fetch, and a custom gateway in models.json requires a baseUrl.

Pins how a read line range is displayed in three surfaces (TUI, session tree, HTML export) with the exported viewer run in node:vm, from the RAW string arguments, against a table of normalisations (null offset = from line 1, empty/non-numeric/Infinity limit = no range).

Keeps the generated reference documentation honest: the generated page must equal the committed file (with a message naming the regeneration command), and the set of generated pages is asserted too (#10790).

Pins the remote catalogue overlay: a refresh TTL (3 calls = 2 fetches) with force bypassing it, image/classifier models merged in and unknown types dropped, and a personalised catalogue that may be empty only when the stored list was already empty.

Pins config-value interpolation: literal, $VAR/${VAR}, $$ escape, $! literal and !command; a credential-scoped environment beats process.env; command results (including failures) are cached until clearConfigValueCache, while environment values are never cached; failed/empty commands yield undefined.

Pins theme loading and colour capability: the terminal.trueColor setting beats PI_TRUE_COLOR in both directions, removing the setting returns to automatic detection, and an unsupported theme key produces a path-naming diagnostic that clears once fixed (#9973).

Biggest resource test (1392 lines): extension/skills/prompts/themes/context files, a peerDependencies warning naming the duplicate-runtime-module hazard (#9863), a project's own package.json not owning project extensions, append-system-prompt sources distinguished from literal strings, and loadProjectContextFiles climbing to the repo root including a corrupt gitdir: pointer.
Pins the Bun environment repair: restoreSandboxEnv does nothing off-Bun or when process.env is non-empty, and otherwise restores the environment from /proc/self/environ.
Pins the RPC clear_queue command: the wire command is {type:"clear_queue"} and the response returns both the steering and follow-up contents that were dropped.
Pins the RPC clone command: the wire command is {type:"clone"} and the response carries a cancelled flag.
Pins the client behaviour when the agent process dies: the in-flight request rejects with "Agent process exited (code=43 signal=null)" instead of hanging.

Interactive RPC example (not a test): RpcClient against the built dist/cli.js, streaming message_update deltas to stdout, one-line tool start/end summaries, and SIGINT aborting a running turn vs exiting when idle.
Pins the JSONL framing: the serialiser does not escape U+2028/U+2029, the reader splits on LF only, CRLF input is handled, and a final line without a trailing LF is still emitted.
Pins the RPC prompt semantics: exactly one response line per prompt command id, clear_queue returns both queues it dropped, and clearing the queue does not start an extra turn (one agent_start).

End-to-end RPC test against a real agent process (skipped without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/TOKEN): state, session file contents, manual compaction, bash output entering the LLM context, thinking-level cycling, getEntries with a since cursor (append-only, unknown cursor is an error) and the session tree.

Pins the runtime credential overrides: an override masks the stored key without persisting, list() exposes only {providerId,type}, operation signals are forwarded, and a cancelled delete leaves the runtime override in place.
Pins the scoped-models picker: "enable all" is null rather than an explicit list, toggling one off materialises the list, and re-enabling the last disabled model restores the null (all) state.

Pins the fullscreen theme: scrollbarTrack/scrollbarThumb fall back to muted/text and searchMatchBg/searchMatchText to selectedBg/text when absent, with explicit colours rendered to exact ANSI sequences.

Pins the provider identity: the detailed User-Agent plus provider-specific attribution headers, attribution turned off by the telemetry setting or PI_TELEMETRY=0, and a configured provider header overriding the session header pi would inject.

Manual probe (not a test) measuring OpenAI Codex prompt-cache behaviour through a tool loop: append-only multi-turn prompting, per-subrequest usage logging, monotonicity check on cache reads, switchable SSE/WebSocket transport and the WebSocket cache/full/delta request counters.

Pins createAgentSession defaults: the persisted session path lives under the agent dir keyed by a sanitised cwd, an explicit sessionManager wins and its cwd is derived (and lands in the <cwd> prompt block), and the bash tool can read PI_SESSION_ID/PI_SESSION_FILE/PI_PROVIDER/PI_MODEL/PI_REASONING_LEVEL.

Pins the SDK skills option: skills are discovered by default, an embedder can supply its own ResourceLoader (a structural interface with a synthetic skill), and a loader returning none yields an empty skill list.

Pins the stream options handed to a provider: the before_provider_headers hook sees the assembled header set and its transformation is applied, not forwarded to the provider as a transformHeaders callback.

Pins context edits: a null edit removes a target from the model projection only (the transcript and the original entry are untouched), the latest edit per target wins, string replacements are normalised for array-only roles, and compaction is prepared from the EDITED projection so removed content cannot re-enter the summary.

Pins a missing session cwd: getMissingSessionCwdIssue reports {sessionFile, sessionCwd, fallbackCwd}, an explicit cwd override clears it, and MissingSessionCwdError is raised BEFORE the runtime factory is called.
Pins --session pointing at a non-session file: a friendly single-line error with no stack trace, exit code 1, and the target file's content left unchanged.
