Pins the read-only session id and the fork-target check: a --session-id selects without rewriting, an existing fork target is refused with exit 1, and the fixtures are realpath-resolved because the spawned CLI sees the physical path.
Pins SessionInfo.modified: it is the last user/assistant message timestamp, not the file mtime, so a backup or editor rewrite cannot reorder the list.

Pins entry-to-context projection: the thinking level and model are recovered from the entries that recorded the change, a compaction replaces the messages before firstKeptEntryId with its summary, an unknown leafId falls back to the last entry, and an orphaned entry truncates the context instead of throwing.

Pins session ids: a custom id must be non-empty and alphanumeric (explicit error message), otherwise a UUIDv7 is minted; the file name is timestamp_id.jsonl; a fork always mints a new id and records parentSession.

Pins the on-disk session format: malformed lines are skipped and valid ones kept, an unterminated final record is repaired by appending a newline to the file, the file is written only after the first assistant message, and later entries are appended without rewriting earlier ones.

Pins labels: a label is an entry with its own id and timestamp, the last label change wins, clearing uses undefined, labels live on tree nodes, labels are not part of the model context, a branched session keeps the copied labels, and labelling a missing entry throws.

Pins restoring from preloaded entries: the tree is rebuilt (not flattened), new ids never collide, labels and compactions are resolved, a header among the entries overrides the options, entries with an older header version are migrated while headerless entries are adopted as-is.
Pins the v1 to v3 migration: the header gains version 3 and entries gain 8-character ids and a parentId chain, and the migration is idempotent.
Pins the custom entry kind: it occupies a slot in the branch (parentId chain) and is visible in the entries and the tree, but is excluded from the model context.

Pins the append operations: every append (message, thinking-level change, model change, compaction, custom) takes a slot in the parent chain, a compaction entry records firstKeptEntryId/tokensBefore/usage, and a branched session writes its file immediately when the branch point is a user message.

Pins the session picker's delete affordance: Ctrl+Backspace is not delete while a search query is non-empty, the current session cannot be deleted, and the check works through symlinked aliases of the same file.
Pins the picker rename mode: the hint shows only in the interactive /resume picker, Ctrl+R enters rename mode, and the submitted name is the typed text prepended to the old name.

Pins the picker search and sort: quoted phrases and re: regex filters, an invalid regex yields an empty list, recent preserves input order while relevance sorts by score with a modified-desc tie-break, and the name filter (all/named) runs before the query.

Pins session sharing: concurrent exports are isolated (each own file), a user who chose gist gets a gist without the Radius provider being consulted (#10870), and Radius without authentication errors without spawning gh.
Pins settings diagnostics: a broken settings file reports its path, a store without paths falls back to the scope, and diagnostics are deduplicated by type and message.

Pins external-edit preservation: only the fields explicitly modified in the session override file values on save (the mechanism is stated in the file's header comment), per scope, while an in-memory change to a touched field still wins.

Pins the compaction settings: each field resolves independently through global then project then model override, the provider/model key must match exactly (a provider/* wildcard loses to an exact match), missing fields fall back to the built-in defaults, and 0 is a valid value rather than unset.

Pins the settings manager: external edits are preserved across an unrelated write, invalid values fall back to the default, the renamed uiMode key is not recognised, the external editor resolves by setting then VISUAL then EDITOR then platform default, and shellPath expands ~.

Pins the settings picker: the cycle includes a configured custom value (#9758), the share-destination cycle is gist/radius/auto, and the configured theme and per-model thinking level stay check-marked while browsing.

Pins the shell existence check: access(F_OK) rather than existsSync because a runnable Microsoft Store alias passes access but fails existsSync's extra stat (nodejs/node#36790), applied on every platform, and an explicitly configured missing shell throws.

Pins the skill contract via the fixtures: a name/directory mismatch is allowed, an invalid or over-long name is a warning, a MISSING description means the skill is not loaded, unknown fields are ignored, and a name collision keeps the first skill with a warning naming the other path.
Pins --name persistence: the trimmed name is written to the session before the model validation fails, the CLI exits 1 with no signal, and the session_info entry is what carries the name.

Pins the status indicators: the editor top border is unchanged unless embedWorkingStatus is set, an embedded label keeps the border's visible width exactly equal to the terminal width for widths 1..120, the retry countdown sits in the same border, IdleStatus renders two blank lines, and a disposed indicator stops its timer.

Pins stdout hygiene: with stdout redirected --help prints Usage to stdout, but --mode json --help keeps stdout completely empty and routes even the usage text to stderr so third-party startup chatter cannot corrupt a JSON consumer.
Manual debug script (not a test): streams a real fixture's thinking text in 10-character chunks into a real terminal to reproduce a streaming-rendering bug; no assertions, ends with process.exit(0).

Bash persistence characterization: idle bash results are recorded immediately as a bashExecution message; during streaming they are deferred (hasPendingBashMessages true) and flushed before the next prompt; abortBash cancels running executions and an older execution settling does not clear the newer running state; bashExecution messages emit no message_end; an aborted assistant message is persisted with stopReason "aborted"; ANSI/OSC sequences split across output chunks are stripped and an incomplete multi-byte char is flushed as U+FFFD.

turn_end / agent_before_settle boundary contract: an extension may replace the turn's entries (compaction with firstKeptEntryId null, context_edit replacements, custom entries) and ask for continue:true; the replacement input survives threshold compaction verbatim; entry_appended notifications see the refreshed canonical context; a pre-settlement follow-up is deferred past the explicit continuation; a stale pre-compaction usage figure does not trigger compaction; length-stop recovery is bounded to one compact-and-retry and a distinct queued follow-up gets its own recovery budget.

Codemode tool behaviour: codemode.mode on/only decides whether a tool is declared inline or listed inside the codemode description; hidden tools' guidelines move to describeTool(); nested calls run in parallel and only the script result is returned; nested usage is added to the codemode result; images attach in output order after their saved path; script failures are results that keep partial output; timeout_ms, memory limit and output truncation with a spilled full text; store() writes persist as custom entries and reload from the branch; the codemode model list classifies with catalog auth only. (Read head 210 lines + full test-title index; the remaining ~800 lines were not read line by line.)

Per-model compaction policy: manual / pre-prompt / post-run / overflow all resolve settings.compaction.modelOverrides["faux/faux-1"] and hand the merged {enabled,reserveTokens,keepRecentTokens} to session_before_compact; switching to a bigger model applies that model's policy without changing the global defaults; the model identity is captured BEFORE awaiting summarization auth so a model change during auth cannot swap the summarizer.

Compaction characterization: an extension-provided summary is persisted with its usage and folded into the session stats; system state is checkpointed and summarized/retained system patches folded into it; the summarization request is a STANDALONE context (no agent transformContext, no tools, cacheRetention "none", its own sessionId) framed by a "# Conversation" markdown boundary; a length stop below the output limit does not compact; overflow recovery is attempted exactly once and reports "Context overflow recovery failed after one compact-and-retry attempt"; stale pre-compaction usage is ignored; an error message uses the last successful usage for the threshold check.

MCP OAuth end to end: browser sign-in, proactive refresh of an expired token before the request and refresh after a 401, sign-out that makes the next call an error; a pasted redirect URL works when the browser cannot reach the loopback callback; session shutdown cancels a stalled sign-in and closes without refreshing an expiring token; callbackUrl/scope/clientName/application_type are honoured; `pi mcp login --timeout` gives up even while the authorization server hangs; credentials written by `pi mcp login` are used on the next turn.

MCP integration over an in-memory transport pair: --tools/--exclude-tools filtering of MCP tools, codemode-only MCP tools hidden from the model but callable from scripts, tool_search deferral and activation, per-tool exposure overrides, resource tools, server instructions rendered into the codemode description, waiting for servers that are still connecting (bounded by startupWaitMs), and re-declaring tool_search-loaded tools after resume/reload. (Read head 232 lines + full test-title index; the remaining ~1040 lines were not read line by line.)

setModel persists a model_change entry and emits model_select, and writes the global defaults only when persist:true; the persisted thinking level survives the model's own clamp; a per-model override beats the global default; cycleModel/cycleThinkingLevel are session-only by default; setModel without configured auth throws "No API key for ..."; tool_call handlers can block execution, tool_result handlers can replace content AND usage, context handlers can rewrite the provider messages without changing the stored ones, input handlers can transform or handle input, before_agent_start can inject a custom message and modify the prompt, and reload emits session_shutdown then session_start.

Prompt characterization: idle prompt, tool-call turn, several tool calls in one response, image attachments normalized with the model chosen by before_agent_start; skill commands and prompt templates are expanded before the prompt is sent; extension commands are dispatched without consuming a provider response; a prompt during streaming without streamingBehavior throws a message naming steer/followUp and one during manual compaction throws "Cannot submit a prompt while compaction is in progress"; a run started by sendMessage({triggerTurn:true}) keeps ONE system prompt for every request of the run and a message queued during before_agent_start joins the starting run.

Steering and follow-up queues: an extension command is dispatched immediately when idle; a steer message is delivered BEFORE the next LLM call while a follow-up waits for the current run to finish; one-at-a-time vs "all" batching modes; custom messages with deliverAs steer/followUp/nextTurn; pendingMessageCount is already decremented when message_start fires; queueing an extension command with steer/followUp throws and names the legal alternatives; a follow-up queued during agent_end is delivered.

Retry and event ordering: transient errors retry with auto_retry_start/auto_retry_end, agent_end carries willRetry, an abort during a retry resets retryAttempt to 0, exhausted retries emit a failure, abortRetry cancels the sleep, a retry that recovers into tool calls waits for the full loop, a non-retryable error (invalid_api_key) is not retried, extension events fire BEFORE public subscribers, and the exact event order of a plain turn and of a tool-call turn is pinned.

AgentSessionRuntime: session replacement settles the outgoing session first (the interrupted tool call gets a persisted tool result instead of dangling); importing a file with the same name never overwrites the stored session; new / resume / fork emit session_before_switch or session_before_fork -> session_shutdown -> session_start and honour cancellation; forking an unsaved session reports why; a fork duplicates the active branch (on disk and in memory); a cross-cwd switch updates the runtime cwd; the destination session restores its model and thinking state.

A tool may call other tools by any name through the extension API: `exposure` decides whether a tool is only reachable from other tools, prepareLoadout rewrites descriptions and hides declarations, ctx.executeTool runs the nested calls, a recursive self-call fails with "Tool run_tools not found", the nestedCalls record carries parent/child ids and is persisted, and codemode/tool_search stay inactive until they are named.
The tool-result image normalizer is called with the image settings AND the current model's resize profile, so a model's inputLimits decide the resize rather than a global constant.

The shared suite harness: registers the faux provider, builds an in-memory AgentSession rooted at a temp cwd, captures every session event in an array with an eventsOfType filter, provides a no-op extension UI context, and exports helpers to read user/assistant texts and the last tool result.

Ingestion boundaries are lax on purpose: a tool result with no content, a message_end replacement with null content, a custom message with null content and a session entry loaded from disk with null/missing content are all normalized to an empty content array so they never reach rendering, compaction or provider conversion.

A test MCP server with its own authorization server (discovery, dynamic client registration, PKCE, refresh, RFC 9207 iss, CIMD, a mismatched redirect path) and a `stall` set that accepts requests and never answers them, used to exercise the sign-in timeout and the shutdown path.

The rules of the new suite: use test/suite/harness.ts and the faux provider, never a real provider API or network call, keep the tests CI-safe and deterministic, and do not extend the legacy test/test-harness.ts path unless a missing capability forces it.
A tool call to an MCP server that has not connected (or never will) still renders with the MCP renderer instead of the expanded fallback, and the same holds in the HTML export.
The pi-ai /models subpath must be present in the extension virtual-module map, and the legacy @mariozechner scope must resolve to the same module object.
Pre-prompt recovery of a resumed length stop omits the truncated tool CALL and its tool result together from the next request - never an orphaned tool_result.
Persisted assistant/toolResult order survives a slow extension message_end handler, and the tool_call hook runs only after the assistant tool-use message is already settled in the session.
An extension-origin queued slash-command follow-up is delivered as RAW USER TEXT and does not dispatch the command - the command surface is only for direct prompts.
After a reload the settings are re-read: a prompt template excluded by a newly written settings.json is gone from the session, so the reload does not keep stale resource settings.
Skill name collisions resolve project > user > package, and the collision diagnostic names the package skill as the loser.

fs.watch() must have an error listener: the test spawns a child process, finds the FSWatcher among the active handles and emits a synthetic error; an unhandled 'error' event on an EventEmitter kills the process.
A tool allowlist filters EXTENSION tools as well as built-ins, and an empty allowlist renders "<tools>\n(none)\n" in the prompt.

A replaced session rebinds the extensions BEFORE withSession runs, the callback receives the replacement context, and a captured old ctx/pi from the previous session THROWS instead of silently addressing a dead session.
Reordering the scoped model list is propagated back to the session state, and the /model scoped tab renders the models in the session's order.
The find tool's fd invocation must switch to full-path mode when the glob contains a slash, otherwise every directory-prefixed pattern silently matches nothing.
Each .gitignore must apply to its own subtree only; collecting every .gitignore into one --ignore-file leaks sibling-directory rules.
A transient "Network connection lost." provider error is retried (auto_retry_start carries the message, auto_retry_end succeeds).
noTools:"builtin" disables the built-in tools but leaves extension tools ACTIVE, while noTools:"all" disables everything; the tool surface is not one list.
Settings supplied in memory survive a direct reload, a DefaultResourceLoader reload, and an unrelated setter + flush + reload cycle.
setSessionName emits session_info_changed - both from AgentSession.setSessionName and from the extension API - and extensions receive it too.
When session_before_tree cancels navigation, the branch-summary/compacting state is cleared and the active leaf is unchanged.
An extension's message_end handler may replace the finalized assistant usage cost, and the override is visible both in the session message and in the message_end event.
A tool call that was rendered from the transcript but never resolved stays registered as pending so the live completion event can update it; a call that already has its result does not stay pending.

On SIGTERM the session_shutdown event (runtimeHost.dispose) must be emitted BEFORE any terminal write, while the interactive quit path keeps the opposite order to preserve the final TUI frame; a re-entrant shutdown is a no-op and a dead terminal (EIO/ENOTTY) exits quietly without recording a crash.
The exclusion list wins over the allowlist, filters built-in AND extension tools out of the prompt, and both lists accept glob patterns ("*_tool", "ask*").
Output callbacks that arrive after the bash operation has resolved are ignored - the recorded output must not grow after the fact.
Both session_before_compact and session_compact carry the reason (manual / threshold / overflow) and the willRetry flag, so an extension can tell why a compaction happened.

waitForChildProcess re-arms its grace timer on every chunk, so output written more than 100 ms after exit by a detached descendant is still captured; a genuinely idle held-open handle still releases after the grace, proved with virtual timers.
The login dialog keeps each prompt's own value and the auth instructions / neutral links / setup details when a later prompt appears, so two OAuth prompts do not overwrite each other.
Exporting with a configured theme that does not exist falls back to the active theme and still produces the HTML file.
An UPPERCASE value in models.json (an env var name such as CUSTOM_API_KEY, or a header value BEARER) stays a literal through the startup migrations and is not lowercased into an env lookup.
The signal handlers stay registered until the async terminal cleanup finishes, because signal-exit re-sends SIGTERM when it observes no other listener during the same dispatch.
An unknown RPC command answers with the SAME request id and a "success: false" error, so a client can correlate the failure.

On session replacement the state is rendered and the agent is SUBSCRIBED before the new session's session_start handlers can notify or send a message, so a handler's message is not lost; the same ordering holds for /reload.
Newlines in a session name are filtered out, from both the session API and the extension API.
A tool_call handler may block AND terminate: the tool never runs, the result is an error, the run stops, and the pending provider response is left unconsumed.
Explicit provider "you can retry" guidance (the OpenAI request-id text and the Bedrock JSON envelope) is classified as retryable.

relativizeFindResultPath handles a Windows drive root and the POSIX root without eating the first path segment, keeps a trailing slash for directories, and does not relativize a sibling directory that merely shares a name prefix.

A tool that calls pi.setActiveTools changes the offered tool set BEFORE the next provider request of the same run, the refreshed system prompt is reported during the run, and a before_agent_start prompt override survives the change.
An inline extension with no name is displayed as <inline:N> (1-based), a named one as <inline:name>, and the hidden flag is preserved.
Branch summarization still runs when the request auth has no API key - the summary goes through the ambient stream function and its cost is recorded on the branch_summary entry.
Exactly ONE agent_settled event is emitted per run, after the automatic retries, with ctx.isIdle() true; a follow-up queued by an agent_end handler is delivered BEFORE settlement.
killProcessTree falls back to <SystemRoot>\System32\taskkill.exe (defaulting to C:\Windows) and CONSUMES the spawn error instead of letting it become an unhandled 'error' event.

The summarization call reuses settings.retry (bounded, exponential backoff, gated on a retryable error) and emits summarization_retry_scheduled / summarization_retry_finished; a non-retryable error (insufficient_quota) is not retried, maxRetries is honoured, and abortCompaction interrupts the backoff.
The compaction request must use the AUTH-RESOLVED baseUrl (an OAuth refresh that points at a different host), not the catalog baseUrl.
A DNS lookup failure wrapped in a stream-cancellation message ("getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND") is still classified as transient and retried.
An enabled model with no catalog entry is shown struck through and marked [unavailable], can be removed, and does not clear the rest of the scope.
Opening /model re-reads models.json, so a catalog rewritten while pi is running shows the new provider and drops the old one.

An interactive login is not held behind an older stalled network catalog refresh; the post-login catalog refresh is bounded to 15 s and a timeout is a warning ("using cached models"), while an empty catalog is reported only after the refresh.
A length-limited summary is not persisted: compact() rejects with "generation hit the token cap" and no compaction entry is written.
An RPC prompt during a manual compaction is refused with "compaction is in progress" - it is not queued, no user message is persisted, and no agent_start is emitted.
The model selector renders the cached models immediately with a "Refreshing model catalogs…" hint and updates when the background refresh completes; closing the selector aborts the refresh.
An invalid resource field in a package manifest is ignored without dropping the valid fields of the same package.
Extension-owned event-bus listeners are removed on reload and on dispose (the host's own listener survives), and a captured stale extension API throws after a reload.
Typing a filter moves the selection back to the FIRST row of the All tab and of the Scoped tab, instead of staying clamped at the previous index.
A manual compaction requested during an active response aborts that response and PERSISTS it before the compaction entry, so the session file order is aborted-assistant then compaction.
The `--` end-of-options delimiter stops option parsing while @file handling continues; an unknown --flag with a value is captured rather than rejected.
The JSON wire projection of a message update is DELTA-ONLY (no cumulative message or partial snapshot) and its serialized size must scale LINEARLY with the text (2x text < 2.2x bytes).
A stalled availability refresh must not overwrite a newer snapshot or a newer error state when it finally settles - the refresh writes are stale-checked.
An exact model match is resolved from the availability snapshot WITHOUT starting a catalog refresh; only a cache miss spends the caller-owned refresh deadline, and then the status line says so.
Session discovery walks a symlinked (or junctioned) session directory and preserves the alias path in the result; a broken link is ignored without hiding valid sessions.
Nested provider retry settings MERGE across scopes (global + project) instead of being replaced, so a project that sets only maxRetries keeps the global timeoutMs.
A method captured from the TUI reference before a renderer replacement still routes to the CURRENT renderer, and a captured method keeps calling the original one.
A startup diagnostic (e.g. "Invalid settings file ...: malformed JSON") is rendered inside the transcript, not only in a transient overlay.
The delta-only JSON projection still carries the cumulative usage; the fixed-size metadata must not be dropped with the snapshots.
A toolcall_start JSON event carries the tool call id and tool name, and nothing else, so a client can key the call without the cumulative snapshot.

The extension loader is LAZY - jiti and the bundled virtual-module map are not loaded until an extension is actually imported - and in a compiled (SEA) binary the tryNative:false branch takes precedence over the source branch.
A project-local agent needs a per-call confirmation in an UNTRUSTED project ("Canceled: project-local agents not approved.") and none in a trusted one.
When no assistant has reported usage the compaction check falls back to a message estimate, so a zero-usage response can still trigger a threshold compaction.
A UTF-8 BOM is stripped when reading frontmatter and settings files, and a settings write does not put the BOM back.

An extension factory that throws discards its runtime changes (flags, providers, listeners) and its API is deactivated with a message naming the extension; a concurrently loaded factory's provider is not discarded.

A custom message injected while a tool is running is appended AFTER the turn's tool results (never between a call and its result), the session entries and the message events keep the same order, and every tool result in the LLM history follows its tool call.
Toggling the thinking-block visibility mid-run does not discard the partial output of a running bash tool.
A fork during an active tool turn does not append the aborted turn to the replacement session - the new session starts with only its own system message.
When a later tool preflight aborts, NO prepared tool executes and no tool_result hook runs; both calls still end with an error result ("Operation aborted") so the model gets a matched pair.
An extension command may stream from a provider registered with pi.registerProvider() through ctx.modelRegistry.stream / streamSimple, and the provider is not left registered globally afterwards.
A fork that removes a context-invisible label boundary keeps the compaction's context: firstKeptEntryId is re-pointed at the first kept message and the summary still opens the context.

A user_bash handler that throws or returns an unparseable result FAILS CLOSED - bash never executes and the RPC answers success:false with "Invalid user_bash handler result"; only an explicit undefined means "run it normally".
Tree navigation is refused while a compaction is in progress and while another navigation is already waiting, with a message naming the wait; the active leaf does not move.

An abort during post-run auto-compaction prevents the compaction from starting at all; the summarization auth call is abortable; "Compaction cancelled" is an ABORT while an unrelated AbortError is a FAILURE (aborted:false with the message), and an extension's cancel is reported as aborted.
The ordinary (non-SEA) extension loader also defers jiti and the virtual-module map until an extension is actually imported, and keeps tsconfigPaths on.

A context handler that slices from the compaction summary does not lose the prompt or the tool declarations (the system head and tools are re-attached); mid-conversation system messages stay in place; a handler may edit event.messages in place; context_with_system runs after context on the restored transcript and its output is sent verbatim, and a handler that drops the leading system message is REPORTED through onError while its output is still honoured.
A real 413 from a gateway (a request-size overflow, not a token overflow) is answered by COMPACTING the image-heavy history and retrying; the retried request no longer carries the images.

loadExtensionsCached caches the extension MODULE per cwd but re-runs the factory on every load; loadExtensions (direct) is never cached; a resource-loader reload clears the cache; the cache is scoped to one cwd.
A pre-prompt compaction of a length-stop overflow does not continue from the truncated assistant message - agent.continue is never called and the next prompt is a fresh turn.
An overlapping startup and replacement rebind does not subscribe twice: the stale startup rebind must not subscribe to the agent or update the terminal title.
Tree navigation during an active response is refused ("Wait for the current response to finish before navigating the session tree") and the active leaf does not move.

A virtual model is a STABLE SELECTION that routes every request; the route reason is one of user / retry / continuation / direct and the request carries the failed model and the previous model; the context limit and the compaction threshold come from the PHYSICAL model that produced the last response, not from the virtual one; the router's state is persisted on the branch as a custom entry.

Syntax highlighting loads the twenty common languages at startup and defers the rest, decodes the HTML entities highlight.js emits, inherits the parent format for unmapped nested scopes, and colours each Python docstring line independently.

The prompt and the tool declarations are written ONCE as a structured head system message (sections + toolsAdded) and reused across the session; diffSystemPromptSections turns two section sets into a per-section PATCH; a forced prompt is sent as the leading prompt for the run and never recorded in the transcript; a tool-set change emits a system patch with toolsRemoved and the refreshed sections before the next request.

The system prompt's exact shape: the default preamble, "<tools>\n(none)\n" for an empty tool set, the <addendum>/<project_context>/<cwd> sections, shell-specific guidance, the docs-path instruction, a tool is listed only when it has a promptSnippet, promptGuidelines are deduplicated and trimmed, skills are listed only when read or bash is available, and hidden tools are left out of the list AND the rules.

The generated "system" theme keeps body text at WCAG 4.5:1 on the background and its panels, orders the foreground roles by contrast, keeps the panels close to the background, uses the terminal's palette hues, keeps pastel palette colours pastel at other lightnesses, and renders as grayscale at zero saturation.

The legacy harness is itself tested: the faux response sequence, tool-call execution, an error response, a pending response turned into an error, retry on a transient error, custom usage numbers, event capture, context capture, response wrap-around, text/thinking/toolcall delta streaming and their order, and the disambiguation of duplicate extension commands into "shared-cmd:1"/"shared-cmd:2".

The legacy harness: a faux stream function with a declarative response sequence (text / toolCalls / thinking / stopReason / error / usage / delayMs / model override) that replays token-level deltas, a state object exposing callCount and the captured contexts, and a one-call factory for a fully wired in-memory AgentSession with an event capture array.
allowNetwork() unsets PI_OFFLINE so a test that replaces external I/O with local fixtures may exercise the network code paths.
A developer CLI (not a test) that prints the built-in themes' contrast against white and black, computes colours at a target WCAG ratio by binary search in HSL, and can audit any theme JSON file.

The interactive theme controller uses the initial theme without persisting it, applies the theme immediately and lets startup wait for the terminal colours (grayscale until the answer arrives), falls back to palette indices and applies a late reply, re-queries on an appearance change and lets the terminal decide, re-renders only when the reported colours actually change, and stops the appearance updates when disposed.

Terminal theme detection: COLORFGBG is classified by palette index like Vim, the background wins over the reported scheme over COLORFGBG over dark, the foreground is followed when that is the readable direction, the colour mode follows the terminal capabilities (256color vs truecolor), and a "light/dark" auto setting is parsed and resolved.
HTML-export theme colours resolve variable references with the same syntax as the colours, convert OKHSL to hex because CSS has no OKHSL, resolve recursive vars and convert 256-colour values to hex.
A custom theme is listed by the name inside the theme file, not by its file name.

theme.style() matches the generic text styler, an unknown token (or a background token in the foreground slot) throws "Unknown theme color: ...", OKLCH and OKHSL values load (including through variables), the appearance is detected unless declared (and palette-only themes follow the terminal background), and an empty token renders as the terminal default while still reporting a concrete colour.
ThemedText builds lazily and rebuilds with the current theme only after an explicit invalidate(), so a theme switch does not silently repaint stale content.
The thinking selector keeps the current level marked while browsing, and the "set as default" binding is the configured one (app.thinking.save), not a hard-coded key.

The tool-execution renderer: non-PNG tool images are converted once the transcoder loads and a replaced partial image does not resurface; custom call and result renderers stack over the built-in shell; a self-rendered empty row takes no layout space; a built-in override keeps the built-in rendering; the bash renderer emits an initial empty partial update, does not duplicate the final truncation details and shows a recorded duration; a missing renderer slot is inherited from the built-in tool; the fallback header shows the arguments; results collapse until expanded. (Read head 120 lines + full test-title index; the remaining ~600 lines were not read line by line.)
An example that registers a custom tool renderer must leave the SYSTEM PROMPT byte-identical to the baseline, and minimal-mode's edit tool renders like the default shell.

Tool-result image normalisation: the original array is returned untouched when there is nothing to do, an oversized image is resized (to 2000 px) and the ORIGINAL dimensions are reported in a note, auto-resize can be switched off, an unsupported format is still converted, an undecodable image is KEPT rather than dropped, and the surrounding text blocks keep their order.

The BM25 tool search: the tokenizer splits camelCase/snake_case, drops stop words and folds plurals; the ranker honours the limit and searches property names and descriptions; an unknown query returns nothing (no synonyms, so "tickets" does not find "issues"); the codemode description catalog fills its budget round-robin, cheapest first, says what is missing, is deterministic, and leaves deferred tools and namespace instructions out.

Each built-in tool's promptSnippet and promptGuidelines must equal its declared system-prompt contribution, and the shell tools' session-environment guidance disappears when exposeSessionEnvironment is false.

Resolving an external tool's latest version reads the release-page redirect (tags without a v prefix are kept, a relative target is resolved, the body is discarded) and a missing redirect fails with a clear message; ensureTool reports through a status callback (never console) and surfaces the whole error cause chain.

The built-in coding tools end to end: read (line/byte truncation, offset/limit, image detection by magic bytes, BMP read as PNG), write (creates parent directories), edit (finds text, refuses ambiguous matches, replaces several disjoint regions in one call, matches against the ORIGINAL file, refuses empty and overlapping edits, never applies partially, and surfaces ENOENT/EACCES in the diff preview), bash (exit codes, a 1 MiB structured-content cap, timeouts, abort, stdin vs -c transport, command prefix, output coalescing, UTF-8 split across chunks), grep and find (global limit, RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH ignored, flag-like patterns treated as text), ls, the ctx.cwd resolution of every tool, and the fuzzy edit matching (trailing whitespace, fullwidth punctuation, smart quotes, Unicode dashes, NBSP) with its CRLF/BOM preservation. (Read head 90 lines + full test-title index; the remaining ~1360 lines were not read line by line.)

The session-tree selector: the initial selection focuses the nearest visible ancestor when the current leaf is a metadata entry (model_change, thinking_level_change), context edits are hidden by default, switching filters re-anchors the selection, the help rows are not truncated on a narrow terminal, ctrl+x copies the full selected message, label timestamps toggle, an empty filter preserves the selection, and folding/unfolding with ctrl+arrow and alt+arrow survives filtering and multiple roots. (Read head 120 lines + full test-title index; the remaining ~620 lines were not read line by line.)
The trigger-compact example auto-compacts only when the context usage crosses its threshold; the turn_end handler is what triggers it.

truncateToWidth measures DISPLAY width, not byte length: checkmarks, emoji and mixed ASCII/wide text are truncated to the visible width, the text is not truncated when it fits, an ellipsis is added when it is, and the exact crash case (a 68-wide line in a 67-wide terminal) is covered.

Project trust decisions are stored per directory and INHERITED from a parent directory (setting null clears the local decision and falls back to the parent); trust-requiring project resources are detected (.pi/settings.json, .agents/skills).

The trust selector shows the saved decision and whether it is inherited, marks the current decision while browsing, selects "Trust" with the path update, and offers "Trust parent folder" which writes the parent as trusted and the child as null.

The user message component keeps a stable height by moving the closing OSC 133 markers off the line end, chains Markdown transformers with a {messageType, isStreaming, availableWidth} context, and reapplies them on invalidate().

Shared test utilities: the API key and ~/.pi/agent/auth.json resolution (including refreshing an OAuth credential and writing it back with 0600), userMsg/assistantMsg factories, readSessionFileRoles, createTestExtensionsResult (naming inline extensions <inline:N> / <inline:name>), createTestResourceLoader, createTestSession for e2e tests, and buildTestTree for building a branching session tree.

The pi version check: versions compare numerically including a beta suffix, only a NEWER version is offered, the pi.dev API is called with a "pi/<version>" user agent, an explicit request retries while an automatic check makes exactly one request, PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK disables only the automatic check, and a nested network error is flattened to "fetch failed (ETIMEDOUT, ENETUNREACH)".

Virtual models in the model runtime: getBranchSelection looks up only the LAST model_change (one catalog lookup, not one per message) and falls back to the latest physical response; a virtual model declares contextWindow 0 and maxTokens 0, its thinking levels are clamped by the resolved physical model, and a failed request is reported separately from the latest successful response. (Read head 150 lines + the full test-title index; the remaining ~290 lines were not read line by line.)
On Windows a legacy WSL launcher under the ACTUAL Windows directory is detected and switched to stdin command transport, while a bash.exe outside the SystemRoot is not.

Release history 1.0.0-1.4.0 written as behaviour changes with issue links; records the removal of TaskRuntime.sleep(), the armed crash-loop guard, the required checkpointWhen predicate, and the prompt-cache baseline bug.

Normative 5618-line specification in 13 sections: core records, documents/Chord deltas, transactions, tasks, scheduler, submissions/inbox, extensions/hooks/tools/system prompt, built-in tasks, document observation, storage contract, backends, API footguns, non-goals.

Package manifest for @earendil-works/pi-durable 1.4.0: a 19-condition export map splitting env/codemode/tools/images/storage/testing, pinned workspace deps, a two-pass test script and ten standalone bench:* scripts.
Host-facing API tour: ten core concepts, the entry/task diagram of one answered input, one section per feature, and the three error rules that decide what an error does.

Code-mode tool: model-written JS in a QuickJS sandbox that calls tools as nested calls and survives restart via a write-ahead journal plus deterministic replay; issued-count barrier, divergence detection, module-version and sandbox-fingerprint guards.

Builds the code-mode prompt surface: a fixed tool description and a codemode system section listing the callable tools as TypeScript declarations, grouped by namespace and fitted to a token budget, with every namespace represented before any is complete.
Boilerplate barrel: re-exports the code-mode extension and tool factories, the store document, the reserved names and the namespace type, and publishes CODEMODE_MODULE_VERSION.

The models.* globals for code-mode scripts: catalog lookups plus classify and generateImages as internal tools with callers ["tools"], so paid effects get their own durable task, live row, abort and usage accounting; models are resolved by provider and id only.

Formats a code-mode script's result for the model: a header with the wall time, per-item markers, one console_output block, images written to temp files, and a token-budget truncation that keeps the head and the tail and spills the complete text.

Defines the durable document model: defineDoc and defineDocFamily with a typed scope, history and fork semantics, a stable id derived from the logical address, and materialisation through the definition's migrate().
Declares the six transcript entry kinds with their is() guards; each entry's docstring states who writes it and what its model, head and data carry.
Byte-exact UTF-8 decoding helpers: a range decoder that turns off Node's streaming BOM handling and a StreamDecoder that strips a leading mark itself, so decoding in pieces equals decoding whole.

The portable ExecutionEnv contract: a Result return type instead of exceptions, FileError and ExecutionError with stable codes, a FileSystem and Shell covering reads, bounded positional reads, paging, listing, watching, and shell exec with spill and a caller-side tail window.
LineScanner: computes the byte ranges and decoded sizes of a line range of an arbitrarily large file from bytes fed in order, in bounded memory, with an exact first-line size.

NodeFileWatcher: watches by snapshot diff rather than trusting OS events, polls on Windows and on unreliable filesystems, hashes recently modified small files in polling mode, and re-reconciles a watcher when a directory's identity changes.

NodeExecutionEnv: the local ExecutionEnv - a strict-LF line reader, a bounded positional binary reader, a directory reader, shell discovery with Git Bash on Windows and a WSL stdin transport, process-tree kill, and a spill path with backpressure.

Four error types with distinct semantics: an error formatter that never throws, ReadAfterWrite for a table read after the first write, StorageRequestError that fails one read but not the Session, and SessionFailed and ConversationBusy.

Resolves the effective agent: composes extension tools, sections and wrappers, filters by the stored tools and modelTools with a deferred-tool loadout, and defines the default retry, compaction and progress policies and the settings merge.

The compaction task: selects a cut that never separates a tool call from its result, summarises the dropped prefix with a pinned prompt that omits thinking, and places the summary directly or through a write submission.

Derives the active transcript and model context from committed entries: bounds captured on the Session line, a previous range reused, the JSON frozen, tool results ordered after their assistant with a missing one synthesised, and the first system message led only when it is the baseline.

Identity and typing helpers for extension authors - defineExtension, defineTool, section, hook, wrapTool and wrapSection; the rules are that a section key matches a regex and is not the reserved instructions key, and that a hook binds to the task's name.
Translates each commit publication into an ordered batch of agent events by diffing the before and after pi.live view and decoding the Chord view ops into text, thinking and tool-call deltas.

The generation task - the harness's agent loop: prepare, request, classify (deferred poll, tool round, answer, overflow compaction, retry) and the tools phase, with every assistant entry written through appendAssistant so the usage stays complete.

Harness.open and the Conversation handle: root, fork and independent creation, submit, compact, reset, abort and waitForIdle, the rule that only the Harness writes model context to a busy conversation, the invocation-bound handle, and the failure containment.

The durable input queue: prepareBoundary and applyBoundary at the postTools and final boundaries under the steering and follow-up modes, and a write whose head points before the active range marked stale rather than applied.

assignJson: assigns a value leaf by leaf into an existing container so Chord records a string reassignment as an append instead of a whole-container set - the mechanism that keeps a streamed partial from being republished whole.

The pi.live document: run control, the current generation attempt, the tool round's slots, the nested call slots and the compaction statuses; the checkpoint rule makes a complete base whenever nothing runs.

Prompt planning: replaySections rebuilds the sections in effect, planSystemEntries computes the minimal pi.system patch that makes the replayed sections and tools equal the desired ones, and planTools keeps byte-equal declarations so the prefix stays cacheable.

The provider-facing conversation identity: pi.provider holds a uuidv7 session id, every fork starts with a fresh one, and a legacy conversation is migrated in one commit rather than on the request path.

The extension registry: an immutable published snapshot of installed extensions, their tools, sections and tasks, with duplicate tool names, duplicate section keys, the reserved instructions key and a built-in task name all refused.

The durable task scheduler: the task and conversation ownership tree, phases reserved and run on the Session line, waits validated against the wait-for graph, abort cascades derived from durable intent so a crash repairs them, a task parked at the restart limit, and wake() for the host.

Durable submissions: admitSubmission decides in one commit whether a draft is placed, queued, refused or stale, a display-only write bypasses the queue, a known requestId returns the existing submission, and a steer's span is linked to the running generation's trace.

The live task graph as a replicated Chord state: nodes with status, phase, owned conversations and a blocked reason, the reason re-derived when the registry changes so a task no definition can take shows as blocked without a commit.
The content-free telemetry vocabulary: two spans, three metrics and the event schemas - deliberately no error payloads, only ids and fixed enumerations.

The ToolTask: commits the final arguments and replay policy before running, validates the structured output against the tool's schema, and refuses a nested call re-made with a different tool or arguments.

The harness type surface: HarnessOptions/Settings, Extension, ToolRegistration, ToolControl, the hook interfaces and the TaskRuntime/TaskDefinition contracts; settings getters may be synchronous because some readers run on the Session line.
The pi.usage ledger: model and tool spend added in the commit that records the response, with own-key lookups and defineProperty so a tool named __proto__ cannot reach the prototype.
The Waiters multimap (each wait settles once and detaches its abort listener when it settles), scanAll(), and closedError() which distinguishes a normal close from a failed one.
The conversation view mount: the active transcript plus the built-in documents, advanced from the Session's commit publications, with a document set whole when its incarnation or version changes.
Boilerplate: idFromNumber and seqFromNumber, the only functions allowed to erase the numeric id/seq brands.
A 10-line adapter: createCloudflarePhotonImages() passes Wrangler's compiled WASM module to createPhotonImages(), because Workers cannot compile WebAssembly from bytes at runtime.
Reads the EXIF orientation of a JPEG or WebP from the bytes without decoding, handling both endiannesses and the WebP Exif-prefixed chunk.
The Photon (WASM) image processor: decode, orient, scale and re-encode to fit the limits, with a JPEG quality ladder and a 0.75 dimension fallback; orientations 5-8 are transposed in JS.
The worker thread that runs Photon off the caller's event loop, resolving the WASM itself and correlating requests and replies by id.
The Node image processor: Photon in a worker thread by default with a permanent in-process fallback, a 30s idle exit to reclaim WASM memory, and a ref()/unref() pair around a pending image.
A 5-line ambient module declaration so cloudflare.ts's WebAssembly.Module import type-checks; no mechanism of its own.
The 216-line public barrel: the document/entry/task definitions, the error classes, the harness and its types, createSession, MemoryStorage and the whole type surface.
BM25 ranking for tool search: a camelCase-splitting, stop-worded, naively stemmed tokenizer and Okapi scoring (k1 1.2, b 0.75) whose ties keep document order.
Selects the documents a fork copies: one pass at the fork point with the asOf policy and one at the parent with the current policy, minting new incarnations and refusing an ambiguous address.
The Session-to-Chord bridge: an attachable advancing state source whose frame queue is bounded at 100, after which the consumer receives a root replacement instead of an unbounded buffer.
The Session kernel (1123 lines): one mutation line, the bounded document cache, commit adoption and publication, and the GuardedStorage wrapper that decides which backend errors are fatal.
One commit: document acquisition and retirement, table reads and writes, fork copies and the base/delta plan; a read after the first write throws ReadAfterWrite.
The IndexedDB backend: the same eight stores and seventeen indexes as the SQLite one, one index driving each task scan, and multi-store reads inside a single transaction.
A 6-line barrel re-exporting JsonlStorage, its corruption and poisoned error classes and the options type.
A 14-line adapter: openNodeJsonlStorage() opens a JSONL storage directory over the local Node filesystem.

The crash-safe JSONL backend: big payloads in per-record sidecar files, a small commit marker in the main log, sidecar reclamation after the marker is published, and a poisoned state after a failed write.
The in-memory reference backend: the maps and indexes, a structural deep copy that preserves null prototypes, frozen returns, and a fork-aware head-marker walk up the parent chain.
The shared cursor rules: a cursor carries its own order, a different order is refused, and a malformed cursor is a StorageRequestError that fails only that read.
A 15-line adapter opening the SQLite backend over a Durable Object's SQLite storage, optionally under a table prefix.
A 1-line re-export of the Chord SqliteDatabase/SqliteExecutor/SqliteValue types.
An 8-line barrel re-exporting the Chord SQLite types, the migration helpers and SqliteStorage.
The SQLite schema history: two versions, next_id as TEXT because node:sqlite rejects out-of-range INTEGERs, and a table rebuild for the sleeping status because SQLite cannot alter a CHECK in place.
A 22-line adapter opening a file-backed durable storage over Node's built-in SQLite, validating the table prefix before the file is touched.
The immutable table and index identifier history, so a rename adds an entry and historical migrations keep rendering their original object names.
The SQLite backend: parameterised reads and scans, a transactional document materialisation, JSON-encoded indexed strings to survive surrogate replacement, and a close that drains admitted reads.
An 8-line identity function typing a task definition; the comment says to register it so a Harness can run tasks of its kind.
Adapts a Vitest/Jest-compatible expect to the suite's assertion interface, so the durable package ships cases and the host supplies the runner.
The runner-independent ExecutionEnv conformance suite: file and listing cases, watch semantics, and shell cases that prove the argv form is unparsed and that the output window is exact.
A 27-line barrel re-exporting the assertion adapter, the two conformance factories, the runners, the benchmark helpers and the option types.
Registers the runner-independent conformance cases with a Vitest/Jest-compatible runner, passing a per-case timeout for the watch-latency cases.
A deterministic benchmark dataset seeded through the public Storage contract only, including a fork chain eight deep and several document replay tails, plus the read and write benchmark definitions.

The runner-independent Storage conformance suite (1682 lines): id allocation, fork visibility, head markers, cursor pagination, document incarnations, task and submission lifecycles, id-space exhaustion and post-close rejection.
The option and case types of the two conformance suites and the single assertion vocabulary they share.
The host timer abstraction: nativeTimer waits long delays in steps and unrefs background timers, while hostTimers falls back to setTimeout for a foreground timer the host declines.
A 7-line barrel re-exporting the tool_search extension/tool factories, the default limit and the tool name.
The tool_search tool: BM25 over the deferred tools, loading the matches with control.addTools so the next request offers them; its description is fixed so it does not move when MCP servers connect.
The bash and powershell tools: a nonzero exit is an error result carrying the exit code, a failure throws, output past the limits spills to a file, and a prepare hook can rewrite the command.
The diff and edit-application utilities: LF normalisation with the original BOM and line ending restored, fuzzy matching over a normalised space, and index-aware not-found and duplicate errors.
The edit tool: repairs the argument shapes models commonly send, matches every edit against the original content, and serialises the read-modify-write through the file mutation queue.
An 8-line helper returning the call's execution environment or throwing "No execution environment is configured".
Serialises edit and write mutations of one file within the process, keyed by the environment id plus the canonical path so a create and a later mutation share one queue.
The image-processor contract and limits (2000px, 4.5MiB base64) plus a base64 helper that builds the binary string 8 KiB at a time to avoid a stack overflow.
Header-only image detection and dimension reading: a 32-byte header, a 64 KiB-blocked PNG chunk walk that refuses animated PNGs, and a JPEG SOF scan excluding the DHT/JPG/DAC markers.
The coding-tools extension (read, write, edit, bash), which nothing installs automatically; createPowerShellTool() is exported but deliberately not part of it.
Path resolution for the file tools, including the Unicode-space, narrow-no-break-space, NFD and curly-apostrophe variants tried in order until one exists.
The read tool: a bounded head read, a line-range scan for offset/limit, truncation reported as a diagnostic with the exact continuation offset, and a retry when the file changed while it was read.
The write tool: creates the file and its parents, runs inside the file mutation queue, and checks the abort signal before and after the write.
The shared truncation utilities: 2000 lines and 50KB independent limits, never a partial line, and truncateHeadOf for a caller that has only read a prefix.

The root type contract: branded ids and Seq, the document semantics, the task records and runtime, the query and cursor types, and the Storage interface, including the rule that a phase must commit progress or it faults.

Ambient declarations for the slice of the Workers runtime the workerd lane uses; explains that full Workers types would conflict with Node's, and types the Durable Object storage as SQLite plus a synchronous kv.

Runs the shared storage-conformance suite against SQLite inside a Durable Object with a per-case table prefix, plus a version-1 -> version-2 schema migration that keeps its tasks and its exact index set.

The workerd vitest project: the cloudflareTest plugin with wrangler.jsonc, root set to test-workers/, include *.test.ts, and source-condition aliases for the package root, /testing and the sqlite/cloudflare subpath.

Three serverless-host behaviours: a task that sleeps through an eviction and resumes from its alarm, a turn cut off mid-stream recovered through the heartbeat alarm with the same requestId, and an object that can be evicted despite holding idle documents.
The reference host: a Durable Object that opens a Harness, arms an alarm before resume, keeps its faux script in KV so it survives eviction, and moves the Harness clock with a persisted offset.
Ten-line wrangler config: the SESSIONS Durable Object binding, nodejs_compat, and a new_sqlite_classes migration tag for the SQLite-backed object.
The chat fixture: a faux provider, a registry, live settings and reports; openChat, allEntries (oldest first), textOf, waitFor, unanswered (a response that never answers) and toolsNamed.
Measures code-mode overhead against a plain tool doing the same nested calls, sequentially and in parallel, reporting wall time and commits per call on SQLite.

Pins the built-in code-mode document checkpoint policies: task-scoped documents stay deltas until their task retires, and the codemode store takes a base after 64 deltas without changing historical reads or forks.

Pins the code-mode prompt surface: a constant tool description, the section's namespace-grouped catalogue, the token budget with every namespace represented first, deferred tools found by searchTools, and the grammar-constrained tool declaration.

Pins the models.* namespace: no credentials or headers in the catalog a script sees, classify and generateImages as hidden internal tools with their own usage, shape checks before the request, a four-call concurrency cap, and a note for images the script never showed.

The durable code-mode tool: journal-then-deliver, replay after a restart, divergence detection (a different call count, different arguments, a different end point) ending the call, the sandbox fingerprint guard, timeout across a restart, and the deterministic clock and randomness.
Compares appending to one array document with writing one family member per item, showing the array's per-append copy cost against the family's flat cost.

Property test over 5000 seeded random files: the streaming decoder equals decoding the whole input for any chunking (including a U+FEFF after an invalid sequence) and the line scanner agrees with decoding and splitting the whole file.
Runs the shared environment conformance suite against NodeExecutionEnv with native and polling watchers, plus the watch directory budget, a multi-chunk binary read and a FIFO refusal.

Mocks node:fs to make the spill stream slow and backpressured, then pins that inherited stdio stays open past the post-exit grace period so a descendant's delayed output is not lost, with the spill file byte-exact.

The Node environment's filesystem, line reader and shell: read/write/list/remove, symlinks, truncation, temp files, aborts, a strict-LF line reader, shell env overrides, timeouts, spawn errors and the spill thresholds.
