Builds win32 x64/arm64 under MSVC or MinGW; MSVC is detected by probing VsDevCmd.bat for cl.exe, the toolchain is forced via PI_TUI_WIN32_TOOLCHAIN, and the temp dir is removed on exit and SIGINT.

Compiled PE/COFF Windows arm64 DLL (MZ header, 9 KB) built from native/win32/src/win32-platform.c; exports napi_register_module_v1, getText, getImage, setText, isModifierPressed and enableVirtualTerminalInput, and resolves the N-API surface through GetProcAddress. Not read line by line because it is a compiled binary - the C source in this shard is the readable form.

Compiled PE/COFF Windows x64 DLL (MZ header, 8.5 KB) built from native/win32/src/win32-platform.c; same seven exported names as the arm64 build. Not read line by line because it is a compiled binary - the C source in this shard is the readable form.
31-line Windows prebuild note; documents the MinGW override env vars and that the opt-in clipboard test replaces the system clipboard contents.
Windows helper: ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT, GetAsyncKeyState modifier probe (general plus left/right virtual keys), and OpenClipboard retried 10 times at 5 ms.
Manifest for @earendil-works/pi-tui 1.4.0; runtime deps are only get-east-asian-width, marked and marked-cjk-friendly, and marked is re-exported so consumers share the TUI's parser.
949-line public API tour; documents the TUI interface, the two renderers, themes, and that TuiAltScreen restores the main buffer and prints the final document on stop.

Transcript search over the rendered screen; buildSearchCorpus strips ANSI and maps flat text offsets to row/column spans, with an ASCII fast path because rendered transcripts are overwhelmingly ASCII.

Combined slash-command / file / argument autocomplete; fd query is built segment-by-segment with every segment regex-escaped, quoted paths keep their opening quote, and applyCompletion has a distinct rewrite per completion kind.
Color values (indexed / rgb / oklch), parsing, mixing and ANSI emission; every color is convertible to sRGB so color math never fails, and styleText closes resets in reverse order.
Transient toast messages composited by the alt-screen renderer; renders nothing into the layout and its timers are unref()ed so a pending flash cannot hold the process open.
Padding+background container; children are rendered unpadded so the cache check is a per-line identity comparison, and the background fn is detected by sampling it with the literal "test".
Loader that aborts on the shared tui.select.cancel binding and exposes a standard AbortSignal, so the cancelled work need not be the loader's own.

2473-line multi-line editor: word wrap, undo, kill ring, history, autocomplete; large pastes become [paste #N] markers that segmentWithMarkers merges into one atomic grapheme, and stale autocomplete responses are dropped by a text/line/col snapshot check.
Horizontal stack; measures each child's widest rendered line, allocates widths, re-renders at the allocated width and composites rows via compositeTuiLine, with align implemented as a row offset.

Inline image widget; Kitty-only PNG conversion via an injected transcoder with a 32-entry LRU whose failures are not cached, and a text fallback that shortens the path and hyperlinks it to file:// when OSC 8 is available.
Single-line input with horizontal scroll, bracketed-paste reassembly, undo and kill ring; the cursor is drawn by replacing the grapheme under it with renderFakeCursor and prepending CURSOR_MARKER.
Animated indicator built on Text; a host-supplied indicator renders verbatim while the default frames are coloured, and an empty frames array hides the spinner entirely.

Markdown renderer; extends marked with a strict ~~ tokenizer, a LaTeX tokenizer that emits a pending token for an unclosed delimiter, and a heading-specific style context so inline tokens restore heading styling after their own resets.
Adds mouse handling to an existing component; the child gets first refusal and the region handler only fires when the child did not handle the event.

Scrollable viewport; follow-end is sticky in both directions with followSuppressedAtEnd, the scrollbar is hidden|auto|always, and disableFollow stops a programmatic scroll to the end from re-arming follow.
Command picker; the description column stays aligned even when the primary text is truncated, and truncatePrimary is a callback so the host decides how to elide.
Settings list with value cycling, nested submenus and optional fuzzy search; Space only toggles until a search query exists, and a submenu's done() can navigate the cursor to a named row afterwards.
28-line stateless widget that renders N empty lines; invalidate() is a no-op with an explicit comment.
The flex-like allocator; growth is weighted by the grow factor but shrinkage by shrink*size so a larger pane gives up more, and each distribution step moves at least one unit and terminates.
Multi-line text widget; the horizontal margin is reduced when the width cannot fit it, and flattenLines is applied so the cached lines are flat strings rather than rope trees.
Single-line truncating widget; emits the ANSI reset before the ellipsis so a truncated styled string does not leave the style open.
33-line vertical stack; the real size algorithm is in stack.ts, and the component's own render passes availableSize undefined so the layout engine is the only constraint.
Capability-based interface for a custom editor (vim/emacs mode); every advanced feature is optional and getExpandedText falls back to getText for editors that do not use paste markers.

Fuzzy match and filter; the score rewards consecutive and word-boundary hits, and a swapped-alnum retry lets "codex52" match "gpt-5.2-codex"; fuzzyFilter splits on whitespace and slashes and requires every token to match.
195-line public surface; exports marked so consumers share the TUI's Markdown tokenizer, and exports isViewportTUI so a viewport renderer is detected by symbol rather than instanceof.

Global keybinding registry keyed by action id; a user rebind never evicts another action's default because eviction only considers user claims, and user-vs-user conflicts are reported by getConflicts.

Key parsing and matching across legacy, CSI-u and modifyOtherKeys; the base-layout fallback is used only when the codepoint is not a recognized Latin letter or symbol, and a logical shifted-symbol match consumes the implicit Shift Kitty reports.
Emacs kill ring with accumulate/prepend semantics; peek does not mutate the ring so yank-pop has to delete the yanked text separately.

1506-line LaTeX-to-Unicode renderer; unsupported syntax returns undefined so the caller can fall back to the raw source, and multi-line constructs are carried as layout markers expanded by renderLayout.
The opt-in layout protocol; LAYOUT_NODE is Symbol.for so the protocol survives duplicate installs, and visible(viewport) lets a stack child disappear without consuming space.
Builds a layout tree with clip rects and a per-(component,width) render cache, so a re-layout at the same width reuses the identical string arrays and the check is an identity comparison.
13-line safe wrapper around the native modifier probe; any failure returns false so a missing addon cannot break the input path.

Computes the native prebuild candidate paths; the first candidate is the installed package root (for bundled apps) and the rest are standalone-binary fallbacks, with the resolution inputs injectable for testing.

Loads the native helper at runtime; the clipboard contract distinguishes undefined (unavailable) from null (empty) from rejection (transfer failed), and the module cache stores loading results, not availability.

Attributed port of Ottosson's Oklab/OKHSL reference implementation; max saturation is a per-channel polynomial fit plus one Halley step and the chroma curve is a two-piece fit through c0, cMid and cMax.
OSC 7501 encoder; control characters are replaced because terminals discard reports containing them, and the message is base64-encoded after a UTF-8-boundary truncation to 2048 bytes.

Re-assembles chunked stdin into complete escape sequences with type-specific completeness tests, and a terminal-reply header pattern keeps a fragmented OSC reply from being delivered as an Alt keystroke.
Parses OSC 10/11/4 colour replies and the colour-scheme report; accepts 6- and 12-digit hex, and the palette is only set when all sixteen replies arrived.

Capability detection and Kitty/iTerm2 image encoding; tmux is probed with client_termfeatures rather than guessed, the Herdr check precedes the Kitty one because KITTY_WINDOW_ID leaks into its panes, and PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP dimensions are read by hand from the header bytes.

Terminal interface and ProcessTerminal; the Kitty handshake is response-driven using a DA1 sentinel every terminal answers, a split reply is buffered and flushed as input after 150 ms, and drainInput stops key-release events leaking to the parent shell.

1797-line alternate-buffer renderer: layout tree, application-owned scrolling, mouse selection with word granularity, transcript search, Kitty image placement and a scroll-to-end indicator; the render pipeline order is resolveFakeCursors, search, indicator, overlays, slice, selection, flashes.

Main-buffer renderer doing differential line updates; a BoundedTerminalWriter chunks output at 1 MiB without splitting a surrogate pair, every frame is wrapped in CSI 2026 synchronized output, and Kitty image reserved rows expand the changed range.

1543-line core: Component/Container/Focusable, the TUI interface, the overlay stack and its focus-restore state machine, render scheduling with an immediate preemption path for keyboard input, and terminal-reply consumption before user input.
28-line generic undo stack; push stores a structuredClone and pop returns the detached snapshot without re-cloning.

1402-line ANSI-aware cell arithmetic; visibleWidth, wrapTextWithAnsi, truncateToWidth, sliceByColumn, extractSegments and the CJK-aware autocomplete regexes, plus flattenLines, a documented trick that forces V8 to flatten a rope-built cached string.

Velocity-based wheel acceleration with a 5 ms burst guard (one physical notch), a 200 ms gesture end, carried fractional lines, and acceleration disabled on macOS local terminals because the OS already accelerates the wheel.

Pure word-motion functions with an injectable segmenter and an isAtomicSegment predicate, which is how a paste marker moves as one unit; inside a word the cursor stops at the last ASCII punctuation boundary.
Benchmark of the real fullscreen shape (2500 alternating Markdown components) measuring steady frames, one-line scrolling, streaming to the last message and a width change, using a null terminal.
Slash-command ranking and whitespace preservation; the fixture is a skill: command set, so the TUI suite already exercises the extension surface.
Provider contract; the fd suite is conditionally skipped when fd is absent rather than mocked, and it covers dot-slash paths, quoted paths and regex metacharacters.
Reproduces the old startsWith implementation inside the test so the bug stays documented; the original symptom was a width assertion firing on a 300 KB base64 image line.
Reference chat app; editor.disableSubmit prevents a second submit while a response is pending, and /delete and /clear splice tui.children by index.
Colour parsing, OKLCH gamut mapping, OKHSL round-trip and the exact ANSI prefix/suffix ordering produced by styleText.
Prompt history driven by a rebound key; an afterEach restores the process-global keybinding manager so the test cannot leak state.
4380-line editor contract; wordWrapLine is imported directly from the source so the wrap algorithm can be unit-tested, and the paste-marker atomicity and sticky-column suites are the largest blocks.
Terminal-restore-on-exit regression; asserts each restore sequence appears exactly once and that the Kitty pop precedes leaving the alt screen, plus a separate no-double-restore test.

Child-process probe for one native clipboard read; asserts the call returns a Promise, does not block the JS event loop (a 10 ms timer must tick over 5 times in 200 ms), and leaves no child or zombie.
C fixture that includes the production clipboard-worker.h with calloc/free redefined as tracking wrappers, exercising the real executor against a controlled blocking callback without X11.

Driver for the worker fixture; 20 concurrent reads must resolve promptly, the process must exit naturally while the private callback never finishes, and the detached operation must survive worker teardown.
X11 selection owner plus a realloc/free tracking wrapper injected into the production source, making the partial-transfer leak deterministic in a way RSS is not.
7-line fixture that starts a TuiAltScreen and calls process.exit(0) with or without stop(), used to test the exit-restore path.
Fuzzy matcher contract; assertions are on the sign and relative order of the score rather than exact numbers, so the weights can be retuned freely.
Manual image harness; prints the detected capabilities and dimensions before rendering, since image rendering is not reproducible in CI.
Input widget contract; pins the deliberate absence of the backslash-Enter submit escape hatch in the single-line input.
Interactive key logger for manual protocol debugging; shows the negotiated protocol and re-renders every 100 ms because negotiation finishes after the first frame.
Registry contract; pins that rebinding tui.input.submit does not evict tui.select.confirm and that user-vs-user conflicts are reported without evicting defaults.
647-line key contract covering Cyrillic Ctrl+C, Dvorak, Kitty alternate keys, super-modified keys and shifted symbols; layout is treated as a first-class concern.
Table-driven LaTeX contract where the expected values form a real mathematical session, so the suite reads like a document rather than a fuzz list.
Pins the flex allocation arithmetic ("allocates vertical grow space deterministically"), making the distribute tie-breaking part of the contract.
Markdown contract asserting on xterm cell attributes (getCell) rather than strings, which is what catches bold/italic bleeding next to CJK punctuation.
Mouse contract for the interactive components, with a SubmenuHost that mirrors the coding agent's theme submenu and a synthetic TuiMouseEvent factory.
Linux clipboard end-to-end; compiles its own C fixtures (with -nostdlib to match the prebuild's link environment) and runs them against an Xvfb display, skipping when the toolchain is absent.
Native module resolution contract; the candidate list is asserted with deepStrictEqual because the order is part of the contract.
Native helper contract, including an ELF program-header assertion that the Linux ARM64 prebuild's load segments are 64 KB-aligned for 64 KB-page systems.
1203-line contract for overlays that do not capture focus; the focus-restore state machine has many legal orderings and each is pinned, with requestRender(true) so the throttle is not a factor.
Overlay positioning and sizing; the overlay records the width it was asked to render at, which is how the width resolution rules are verified.
An overlay must still be visible when the content is shorter than the terminal; on failure the test dumps the whole viewport.
OSC 7501 contract; asserts both the decoded message and the encoded length, so the base64 expansion limit is pinned too.
An overlay starting inside a wide grapheme must exclude it from the before-segment rather than split it; the ASCII case at the same boundary keeps the old behaviour.
A partial flag must measure as width 2 because streaming shows the first half first and a width-1 measure makes the differential renderer drift.
The self-SIGWINCH refresh must not throw when kill(2) is denied; the test patches process.platform so the Windows branch is genuinely exercised.
A slice starting after a colour open must re-emit the open and the close so the colour does not bleed into the following text.
Allocation-churn benchmark using the V8 sampling heap profiler with minor/major GC collections included, so it measures churn and not retention; two scenarios, static and editor.
List contract using a visible-column-aware index helper, because description alignment is a column property rather than a string property.
Pins that a space inside a search query does not toggle the setting while a lone space before any query does.
Escape-sequence reassembler contract; sequences are fed in deliberately awkward splits because that is the real failure mode, including the fragmented Kitty reply case.
Tab accounting: tabs in text are expanded so a tab-containing overlay cannot wrap to a second physical row, while tabs inside control sequences stay byte-identical.
Colour reply parsing plus the query lifecycle (the promise resolves on the DA1 sentinel); the palette is only complete when all sixteen replies arrive.
Capability detection contract; the environment is fully scrubbed of 15 variables so a developer's real terminal cannot change a detection result.
Terminal layer contract; the escape timeout is 10 ms locally, 100 ms over SSH and overridable, with invalid values falling back rather than throwing.
38-line chalk fixture forcing level 3 so ANSI assertions are deterministic; the README's quick-start imports it as its example theme.
Truncation contract; a truncated string is bracketed with resets and an OSC 8 link is closed when its label is cut, and a 100k-repetition emoji string must not hang.
Widget contract asserting exact visible widths and that the reset precedes the ellipsis, including the empty-text and exact-fit cases.
2100-line alt-screen contract; a RecordingTerminal asserts on the order of terminal events, which is how the WezTerm draw-images-last rule is pinned.
The cell-size query must not steal user input; a bare ESC must still be forwarded as Escape and the CSI 6;h;w t reply must update the dimensions.
An overlay must not leak a style past the last visible column; the assertion reads cell.isItalic() from the next row, the only place a leak is observable.
1024-line main-screen contract; the bounded-output suite asserts that chunking a large render does not change its output, and getCellItalic asserts on cell attributes.
Content shrinking to zero must clear the screen; exercises the explicit-clear path rather than the optional clearOnShrink path.
Manual repro of the viewport-overwrite bug, documenting expected versus actual behaviour and how to reproduce it in a 12-row tmux session.
219-line xterm-headless Terminal implementation; the substrate for renderer tests, exposing sendInput, resize, flush, getViewport, getScrollBuffer, getCursorPosition and waitForRender.
Width contract covering OSC 8 links, OSC 133 zones, APC sequences, tabs in styled text and unterminated escapes (an incomplete CSI is zero-width).
Wheel acceleration contract; expected arrays read like a rhythm ([1,5,5,5] for 20 ms gaps), documenting the velocity curve and the burst and direction-reset rules.
Word-motion contract; a hand-built segmentMap injects a fake segmenter so the atomic-segment (paste marker) case can be exercised without an Editor.
ANSI-aware wrap contract; the assertions are about which reset is emitted, since a wrapped underline must end with ESC[24m and not a full reset that would kill the background.
9-line build config; compiles src only, so the test tree is never published.
